XF Studio authors complete eye-makeup presets, keeps them in a local library, previews them on V and builds a private candidate for one in-game selector. This guide defines how its interface looks and behaves, and how new work composes from the same parts. Every pattern states what it contains, when it appears, how it combines and adapts, and which application action or read-only state drives it.

Implementedin the Studio today (public/index.html)Future direction · not builtroom left in the design; needs actions and discussion firstRuleapplies to all work
01

Foundations

A restrained Cyberpunk: graphite instruments under a single signal yellow, with cyan reserved for live state and the info tone. The only ornament is the bevel — a clipped corner borrowed from industrial labelling. No neon glow, glitch, scanline or fake HUD chrome: atmosphere never costs legibility. Tokens are defined once with light-dark(); a container's color-scheme chooses the theme, so every specimen below renders in either theme and in the side-by-side comparison.

Design principles

Rule
  1. Truth before polish. Never show stale, partial, unverified or preview-only results as ready, packaged or game-tested. Status words come from the application, not from the control.
  2. One accent, one meaning. Yellow marks commitment and focus (primary action, active tab, keyboard focus). Cyan marks what is live or selected. Everything else is graphite.
  3. The stage is neutral. The 3D head and UV map sit on a near-achromatic grey surround, light in the light theme and dark in the dark theme, so colour judgement isn't skewed by coloured chrome.
  4. Every affordance is an action. Buttons, menus, shortcuts, drags and the command palette call the same typed application action and show the same disabled reason.
  5. Panels are tools, not places. Any panel can dock, float, tab or join a magnetic composite; nothing depends on a fixed sidebar.
  6. Density with air. Compact 28 px controls and 32 px rows, but generous section spacing and one idea per section.
  7. Previews are diagrams. Neutral subject, one ink, one light, one frame per row; the 3D view is the true preview.
What
The rules every new screen, panel or control is reviewed against.
When
Before designing a feature and again at review. A proposal that breaks one of these needs an explicit exception recorded in the architecture boundary.
Avoid
Literal franchise tropes (glitch text, chromatic aberration, neon outlines, fake terminals), decorative animation, and colour used only for mood.

Implemented

--bg-panelPanel and header surface
--bg-raisedButtons, cards, inspector strips

--bg-hoverHover
--bg-activePressed, composite bar

--line-strongControl boundaries (≥3:1)
--textPrimary text (≥15:1)
--text-mutedSecondary text (≥6:1)
--text-faintTertiary text (≥4.5:1 on panels)

What
Semantic surfaces, lines, text and state colours. Contrast was computed for both themes: all text tokens ≥4.5:1 on panels, control boundaries (--line-strong) ≥3:1, focus ≥11:1.
When
Always reference a token, never a literal colour. User-authored makeup colours are content and are shown unmodified inside swatches.
Combine
State colours always travel with a word or icon (e.g. a warning badge says “Preview only”), never colour alone.
Adapt
Themes switch by color-scheme; forced-colors mode falls back to system colours for selection and borders.

Preview tokens

Implemented
--pv-groundTile ground: the stage's centre tone, flat
--pv-subjectThe neutral head, face or body
--pv-inkThe choice itself
--pv-shadeHow much shadow darkens ink and subject: a number the colour matrix reads (--pv-shade-light .72, --pv-shade-dark .62)
What
The four tokens every choice preview is coloured from (lib-choice-preview). A preview is stored as channels (feature and subject coverage, light), and one SVG colour matrix per theme (built from these tokens) turns them into colours, so a theme change needs no new picture.
When
Only for previews. A preview uses these tokens and nothing else (later: the V's own colour for the ink, when tinted).
Combine
Inside the Choice preview tile (lib-choice-preview), never on other surfaces: the ground sits in a choice item whose border and states are the choice list's.
Adapt
Light and dark values come from the theme (the colours are light-dark pairs; the shade switches with the theme). Forced colours drop the matrix.
Driven by
The page's filter (installPreviewFilter()) reads them through a probe element and rebuilds its matrix when the theme changes.

Copy and wording

Rule
Before

Point strength blends pigment across the shape. More blend softens differences between nearby points; a zero point may retain some pigment. Edge softness controls the outline separately.

After
What
Plain, calm, second person ("your V", "your game files"): what happens and what to do, never how it is implemented. Use the exact names on the controls, one name per thing (3D view, UV map, version, Settings › Game), and no developer words (host, server, SQLite, budget, provisional, LUT, CLI, MiB, "a Studio choice"). Units a person can judge: %, °, MB, or a 0–100 scale for a length on the face, never a raw "% UV" outside research tools; counts agree with their nouns ("1 preset", never "preset(s)" or "1 entries"); no byte sizes or folder paths in person-facing text. Limits: titles 1–3 words; labels 1–4; buttons 1–3, verb first, "…" when a choice follows; a status line one line (about 70 characters); an inline note one sentence (about 100); a help tip at most two short paragraphs (300 characters); a reason one sentence (about 90); a toast one or two sentences with its recovery button. The full rules and the audit are in research/authoring/ui-copy-and-layout-review.md.
When
Where text goes: what something is or how it works → a help tip on its label or heading; what the person can do now → an inline note on a reserved line or the status line, with the button; a changing state → the status line or the control's own label; a set of facts → a structured display (property list, chips); why a control is unavailable → its reason tip; an outcome → a toast; a designed but unbuilt feature → a disabled control with "Coming soon: " (no empty sections).
Combine
Honesty stays, briefly: "not yet checked in game" is one clause, once per place. Say a state in one place only.
Avoid
Repeating a label in the note under it, explaining what a visible control obviously does, naming a control that doesn't exist, a paragraph under a control, and text that moves the layout when it appears.

Spacing, sizing and density

Implemented
246812162028

Controls 28 px (24 px small) · rows 32 px · tabs 32 px · header 44 px · status 26 px.

What
A 2-px based scale. Panels use 12 px padding and 16 px between sections; related controls sit 8 px apart.
When
Keep one scale step between unrelated groups. Do not invent new heights; lists and menus rely on the shared row height for scanning.
Combine
Sections stack with --sp-6; controls inside a section with --sp-4; a toolbar row keeps --sp-2 between related buttons.
Adapt
Compact workspaces keep control sizes; they change arrangement (tabs, icon-only header actions), not target size.
Driven by
Tokens --sp-*, --control-h, --row-h, --tab-h, --header-h, --status-h.

Bevel, borders and elevation

Implemented
ChipBadge
Card7 px bevel
What
Bevelled corners via CSS corner-shape (top-right and bottom-left on controls; top-right on cards, menus, windows). Borders are 1 px; elevation is reserved for things above the dock: floating windows, menus, toasts and dialogs.
When
Bevel is the only decorative shape. Never combine it with rounded corners or drop shadows on docked panels.
Combine
A bevelled surface never nests inside another bevelled surface of the same size; cards inside panels are bevelled, the panel group is not.
Adapt
Browsers without corner-shape show square 2 px radii — the design must read correctly without the bevel.
Driven by
corner-shape: bevel with --bevel / --bevel-sm radii; --shadow only for layers above the dock.

What
Original 16 px line icons, square caps and mitred joins, drawn for this project. Stroke uses currentColor; filled marks are used only for dots and grips.

Motion

Implemented
Updating 2K140 ms ease-out
What
140 ms state transitions, a sweeping bar for indeterminate work and a two-step blink for updating previews. Drop previews ease 80 ms so targets feel magnetic without lag.
When
Motion only communicates state change or work in progress. Nothing loops except genuine ongoing work.
Combine
Progress bars sit directly under the action that started the work; the status bar holds the makeup textures' readiness, and the 3D view's corner badge adds it where the result is seen only while they update or couldn't update.
Adapt
Motion is identical at every size; reduced-motion users get instant state changes.
Driven by
--dur, --ease and the sweep/pulse keyframes; readiness phase from previewReadiness.
Keyboard & access
prefers-reduced-motion collapses all transitions and animations to 1 ms.

Focus and keyboard

Implemented
What
A 2 px ring in --focus (signal yellow on dark, ink on light) with 2 px offset; inside tab bars and lists the ring sits inset so it is never clipped.
When
Every interactive element shows focus-visible. Pointer clicks do not leave rings on buttons.
Combine
Focus follows the action: after closing a menu or popover it returns to the invoker; after a reorder it stays on the moved row.
Adapt
Identical in both themes and all sizes; the ring colour switches from yellow (dark) to ink (light) for ≥3:1 against adjacent colours.
Driven by
--focus token; roving tabindex in tab strips, rows and menus.
Keyboard & access
F6 cycles header → each panel group → status bar. Shift+F10 or the Menu key opens the same context menu a right-click would.

Stage surround

Rule
Stage · both themes
What
Viewports use the same neutral radial surround in light and dark themes. Overlays on the stage use their own fixed colours (stage chip, stage text).
When
Any panel that shows the head, a texture or a material comparison.
Avoid
Theme-coloured backgrounds behind colour-critical content.
02

Shell and navigation

The shell has three bands: a header that names where you are and holds the few global commitments, a dock workspace that owns everything else, and a status bar that tells the truth about saving, work in progress and preview readiness.

Application header

Implemented
XFStudioBeta
Night market setChrome dusk glow
Verification workspaceChanged since last version
What
Brand (the XF mark, the word Studio and the Beta badge), a breadcrumb of collection › preset following the drawn view's look, the library state chip, the verification label when isolated, and global actions: Undo, Redo and History (grouped; their tooltips name the step each would change, such as “Redo: Move point (Ctrl+Shift+Z)”, and keep the shortcut visible while unavailable), Save version, Package, Commands, Help, Settings, Panels and View preferences. Modules and Layouts buttons are retired; layout tabs occupy the separate full-width row below. The specimen is the live header's fit: move the width to see the stages give way in order.
When
Always visible. Only commands that act on the whole document or workspace belong here; anything about a layer or panel stays in that panel.
Combine
The library chip is the one place the save state shows (G3); no panel repeats it, and the Library panel says what it means in a sentence.
Adapt
The names come first, so the person always sees what they are editing (UI-187): the collection and preset names show whole (up to their own maximum width) wherever the stages below can make the room, and otherwise each keeps at least about 12 characters. To give them that room the header's other items give way one stage at a time, always in this order (header-fit.ts, measured whenever the window, the names, the verification label change): 1 Commands shows its icon alone (Ctrl+K opens the palette anywhere); 3 the verification label shortens to “Verification”; 4 Package shows its icon alone; 5 the word Studio goes (the XF mark and Beta stay); 6 Save version shows its icon alone (Ctrl+S); 7 last, and only when even the 12 characters don't fit, the collection's name goes and the preset's stays (the Presets panel names the collection). A label that gives way stays the button's accessible name and its tooltip. The chip keeps its whole words: it is the save state, and its vocabulary is fixed (c-chips). Its room is kept at its widest word (“Changed since last version”), so a save or an edit that changes it moves nothing: no stage depends on what the chip says, and Save version stays where it was clicked. Room the stages leave over goes to the space before the actions, never to a name. Below 720 px the chip and the verification label hide (the Library panel's sentence still says whether your work is saved).
Driven by
library.summary(), authoring.capability({kind:'history.undo'|'history.redo'}), authoring.history(), authoring.requestCapability({kind:'save'}), status.snapshot().verification, preferences.

Feature focus from layout tabs

Implemented
What
The Modules button, category label and menu are retired. A module's tools are offered when one of its panel instances is docked in the shown tab, including a floating or collapsed group. Closed panels do not activate tools. A Poses tab offers no Surface controls; makeup keeps drawing on V in every tab.
When
Use layout tabs and their contributed defaults to choose the work area. Panels opens or closes panels in this tab. Optional experiments follow the tab too.
Combine
Presets and Library belong to Eye makeup. The header crumbs keep following the drawn view's look, regardless of the tab's active tools. The guidance anchor is tabs.strip; no replacement header control is added in phase 2.
Adapt
Feature focus is identical at every header width; the layout strip condenses independently.
Driven by
The shown tab's panel instances and dock arrangement, resolved through panel ownership.
Avoid
Module switches, parked-module rows, a second Layouts menu, or an empty replacement for the retired buttons.

Status bar

Implemented
Gesture in progress · Esc cancels3D view 2K · updating
What
Draft autosave state, restoring's first seconds (“Restoring changes from your last session…”, t-recovering: the line takes them so the workspace notice never opens for a moment), the latest activity or in-flight library message (click opens Activity; “Ready” when there is none, and not while the restoring line shows, which it would contradict), gesture/transaction hints and preview readiness.
When
Always visible. It reports; it never hosts commands other than opening the activity log.
Combine
The message slot mirrors the newest Activity entry; the readiness badge is the steady home of the makeup textures' state (the 3D view shows its own badge only while they update or fail); errors also toast so they are not missed, but never repeat a note the 3D view already shows.
Adapt
Messages truncate with an ellipsis; the Activity panel keeps the full text.
Driven by
status.snapshot().workspace, status.outbox.recovering (shown and not long), library.summary().progress, previewState().gesture/control, previewReadiness.snapshot().
Keyboard & access
Toasts and the activity log carry the same messages to assistive technology through live regions; the status bar itself is not a live region to avoid double announcements.

03

Panel system

Fixed sidebars are gone. Every functional area is a panel that can be docked, floated, grouped as tabs or magnetically joined with other floating panels. Snapping is decided by where the cursor is — never by the dragged panel's size or position — so a large panel passing over others never snaps by accident. The live sandbox and live dock at the end of this section run the production engine.

Docked tab group

Implemented

Presets

Panel content scrolls inside its group.

Colour & finish

Panel content scrolls inside its group.

What
A group shows one panel at a time behind a tab strip. The active tab carries the ink/yellow indicator and a close control; the empty strip to the right is the group's drag handle; ⋯ opens layout options.
When
Put panels in one group when they are used alternately (Presets / Library / Package) and side by side when they are used together (Head and UV map).
Combine
Groups sit in splits. When a strip runs short its tabs condense in stages (the tab strip component, lib-tab-strip): inactive labels cut short, then inactive tabs icon-only (right) while the active label stays readable, then the active one too, then an overflow menu. Every tab keeps its name as its tooltip and accessible name, and the header's collapse and layout buttons never shrink.
Adapt
Wide and compact workspaces keep separate arrangements. In compact layouts, most panels share two groups.
Driven by
Pure layout state (DockTree) saved through the workspace preference action layout.set; no application data.
Keyboard & access
role=tablist/tab/tabpanel; ←/→/Home/End switch tabs, Alt+Shift+←/→ reorders, Delete closes, Enter or ↓ moves into the panel, Shift+F10 opens layout options. Focus inside a group outlines it in cyan.

Help

Panel content scrolls inside its group.

What
Every way of asking for a panel (the command palette, the Panels menu, the Help button, a tour step, a link from another panel) summons it the same way, so it is always shown and focused. Already in an expanded group: its tab becomes active. In a collapsed group: the group expands with its tab active. Not in the layout: it goes back to an obvious home, which is where it was when it was closed (its group at its tab position, beside its old neighbour, or its floating window) or the group it belongs to in the factory layout; with no obvious home it opens in a floating window over the middle of the workspace. It is never dropped into an arbitrary group, least of all a collapsed one (left: Help summoned while the right column's lower group is folded opens floating, right).
When
Always, in the shown layout tab; features never place panels themselves. The Panels flyout lists panels grouped by owner, with open, collapsed and closed states. Choosing an open panel closes it; choosing a collapsed or closed panel summons it. There are no module switches or parked-module rows. With research tools on only, a folded Coming soon heading lists planned modules with their reason; these rows are unavailable. A panel closed by default (Help, Activity) has no home, so it floats until the person docks it; after that, closing and summoning it again returns it to where they put it.
Combine
The Panels menu changes this tab only. Early-access panels carry their Early access tag in their feature's group. A tab's sole unnamed 3D view reads “3D view”; several are numbered within the tab, and renamed views keep their names. Reset to default belongs to the layout tab's menu. Focus moves to the panel's tab, or into the panel when its opener focuses something there (Help focuses its search). The result is announced: “Help opened in a floating window”, “Colour & finish expanded, showing Shape”.
Adapt
The Panels menu stays under its button; when its rows exceed the space below, it scrolls inside. Where a panel was closed from is remembered per size class with the layout (lastPlace); a panel opened by any other route forgets it. A floating panel is clamped on screen like any window.
Driven by
summonPanel(tree, panel, factory, floatRect) in studio-ui/dock/layout.ts, through DockView.reveal. Tests: tests/dock-summon.test.ts.
Keyboard & access
The summoned tab (or the control its opener chose) receives focus; the announcement says where the panel went.

Splits and splitters

Implemented
What
Rows and columns of groups with 4 px splitters. Hover or focus shows the cyan track; dragging resizes the two neighbours only.
When
Any docked arrangement. Minimum group size is 150 × 96 px.
Combine
Splits hold groups or further splits; a group's minimum size stops a splitter before content collapses.
Adapt
Sizes are fractions, so resizing the window scales every column and row proportionally.
Driven by
DockTree split nodes (axis, sizes) via setSizes().
Keyboard & access
Splitters are focusable separators: arrow keys move 4 %, Enter or double-click equalises the pair.

Collapsed group: header row or vertical strip

Implemented
What
A collapsed group keeps only its tab bar. Folded along a column it is a header row spanning the column (right). Folded along a row (a group alone in its row, or a column whose groups all collapsed) it is a full-height vertical strip: the same tab bar turned on its side (left to right: the first tab active, a middle tab active, a shorter strip with the inactive tabs icon-only, and the shortest with every tab icon-only). Each tab has padding at both ends, an upright icon centred across the strip, a gap between icon, label and close mark, and a hairline between tabs; the active tab is raised to the panel surface with the yellow indicator down the strip's outer edge and its close mark as its own 18 px target at its end.
When
Collapse a group to keep its panels one click away while giving its space to the rest of the workspace. Choosing any tab expands the group showing that tab.
Combine
The strip condenses in the same stages as a crowded bar (the tab strip component, lib-tab-strip): full labels, inactive labels cut short, inactive tabs icon-only, the active tab icon-only, then an overflow menu at the strip's end. An icon-only tab keeps its name as its tooltip and accessible name, and a label is never cut mid-glyph. The expand and layout buttons sit at the strip's foot and never shrink.
Adapt
The strip is 36 px wide (the 32 px bar height plus 4 px), whichever tab is active or hovered, so nothing shifts. Its tabs refit whenever its height changes.
Driven by
foldAxes in studio-ui/dock/layout.ts picks the axis; the dock marks the group data-fold and builds its header with orientation: "vertical". The tab CSS is written in logical properties, so writing-mode: vertical-rl on the strip turns padding, separators and the indicator with it. Tests: tests/dock-collapse-dom.test.ts (folding), tests/dock-strip-geometry.test.ts (laid-out geometry in Chrome: no overlaps, padding, centred icons, one width, icon-only fallback).
Keyboard & access
The tablist is marked aria-orientation=vertical and keeps the bar's keys (←/→/Home/End switch tabs). The focus ring is drawn inside each tab (outline offset −2 px), so the strip's clipping never cuts it.

Floating panel

Implemented

Camera

Panel content scrolls inside its group.

What
A panel in its own window above the dock, with resize handles on every edge and corner. Its tab strip is the window's title bar.
When
Temporary tools you want next to the stage without reflowing the docked layout (lighting while judging a finish, Motion while checking closed lids).
Combine
Floating windows can attach to each other (composites) or return to any group. They stay above a maximized group.
Adapt
Windows are clamped so at least their title bar remains reachable after window resize or restore.
Driven by
DockTree.floating windows (x, y, w, h, node) via applyDrop({kind:'float'}), setWindowRect(), raiseWindow() and recoverWindows().
Keyboard & access
Panel menu › Move or resize window… enters a keyboard mode: arrows move (Ctrl for fine steps), Shift+arrows resize, Enter or Escape ends and saves.

Magnetic composite

Implemented
2 panels · magnetic composite
What
Two or more floating groups joined edge to edge into one window. A thin bar moves the whole composite; each member keeps its own tabs and can be dragged out again.
When
When a set of floating tools belongs together (motion + lighting while reviewing on a moving face).
Combine
Join by dragging a panel until the cursor enters the magnetic band along a floating window's edge (18 px either side of the edge) or onto its compass arrows. The composite grows to make room instead of squeezing its content.
Adapt
A composite keeps its members' proportions when resized; if a member leaves, the window returns that member's share.
Driven by
A floating window whose node is a split; created by applyDrop with a split target on a floating group.
Keyboard & access
Panel menu › Place beside › (floating group) › Attach left/right/above/below. Composite menu › Dock composite to edge or Merge into group as tabs.

Drag feedback: cursor targets

Implemented
Motion

The cursor (yellow square) is on the compass's left arrow, so the preview fills the left half: “Split left”. The ghost only labels what is moving; its size is irrelevant.

What
While dragging, the group under the cursor shows a five-way compass (centre = add as tab; arrows = split beside). Edge guides at the middle of each workspace edge dock to the full edge. Tab strips accept tabs at the cursor's insertion point. Floating windows add a magnetic edge band. The cyan preview shows exactly where the panel will land and names the result.
When
Drop outside every guide to float the panel where you release it. Hold Ctrl to float freely even over a guide. Escape cancels the drag and restores a moved window.
Combine
The preview is the contract: whatever it names is what happens on release, and the result is announced to screen readers.
Adapt
Guides are fixed-size (34 px) at any workspace size; edge guides stay reachable in compact layouts; previews are computed from the actual target rectangle.
Driven by
resolveDrop(cursor, geometry) in studio-ui/dock/snap.ts — inputs are the cursor point and the rectangles of target groups/guides; the dragged panel's rectangle is not a parameter. Unit tests assert that a large overlapping panel does not snap until the cursor reaches a target.

Live snapping sandbox

Implemented

Load this guide in a browser with scripts enabled to try the production snap resolver.

Drag the large “Lighting” panel. It only snaps when the cursor — not the panel — reaches a guide.

What
The production resolver running on three sample groups. The dragged panel is deliberately large so it overlaps targets while the cursor stays outside them.
When
Use it to reason about new guide placements before changing snap.ts; keep the unit tests in tests/dock-layout.test.ts in step.
Combine
Pairs with d-feedback: the static specimen explains the vocabulary, the sandbox lets you test it.
Adapt
Fixed 360 px area; resolution uses real measured rectangles.
Driven by
resolveDrop() and previewRect() from src/studio-ui/dock/snap.ts.

Maximized group and empty dock

Implemented

Maximized · Restore button in the tab bar

Every panel is floating or closed.

Use Panels to open one, or Reset to default in the tab menu.

No tabs are open.

Use New tab above to choose a layout.

What
Double-click a tab bar (or use its menu) to maximize a group over the dock; floating windows stay available. If every panel is floating or closed, the dock explains Panels and the tab menu's Reset to default. With no tab, it explains New tab instead and offers no reset (the full U6 state belongs to P2-vi).
When
Maximize for close inspection of the head or UV map; restore the same way.
Combine
The maximized group keeps its tab strip and a Restore button; floating windows stay above it.
Adapt
Most useful in compact windows for the 3D view or UV map.
Driven by
DockTree.maximized via setMaximized().

Keyboard alternatives to docking

Implemented
MotionDocked with Character, Camera & light
Show tab
Float panel
Add as tab to
Place beside
Dock to workspace edge
Maximize group
Close Motion Del
What
Every pointer operation has a menu equivalent on each tab (right-click, Shift+F10 or ⋯): float, add as tab to any group, place beside any group (split or magnetic attach), dock to an edge, maximize and close. Reset to default is in the layout tab menu and restores both size classes.
When
Always available; the command palette also offers Go to/Open and Float for every panel, and the Panels menu toggles each panel.
Combine
The same items appear from the tab's context menu, the group ⋯ button and (for Float/Go to) the command palette.
Adapt
Lists every open group, docked or floating, so it scales with any arrangement.
Driven by
DockView.panelMenuItems() calling applyDrop() with the same targets a drag would resolve.

Menus use roving focus with arrows, Home/End, type-ahead, → to open submenus, ← or Escape to close; results are announced.

Size classes and default layouts

Implemented
What
Each tab and each contributed or own default holds both size classes as independently remembered arrangements. Crossing 1100 px switches between them without losing either. The tab menu's Reset to default restores both size classes from the chosen default. Contributed defaults are read-only; Save as default makes your own. Activity is closed by default and opens from the status bar.
When
Design new panels for both: say which default group they join in each size class. Keep the head's default cell portrait (it is a portrait subject and front framing fits its width) and the UV map's cell wide enough for the 720:310 both-eyes view, with both visible at once.
Combine
Features contribute read-only defaults holding both size classes. Save as default keeps both; Reset to default restores both. An empty tab stays empty.
Adapt
The header condenses labels; the dock does not reflow panels automatically within a size class — users own their arrangement.
Driven by
LayoutFragment.tab.dock, COMPACT_BREAKPOINT and DockState {wide, compact}.

Persistence and recovery

Implemented
What
Tab arrangements persist in the profile session as versioned, bounded workspace data (format xfs/dock, version 1) beside theme choice — never in recipes, collections, SQLite or exports. Own defaults are library documents; legacy layout preferences are frozen migration input.
When
Restored at start through the ui-preferences recovery gate: malformed trees are rejected, unknown panels (a newer build's) kept parked with their places, duplicates removed, missing (new) panels re-added beside their default siblings, and floating windows pulled back on screen. Invalid saved layouts fall back to defaults with a visible notice.
Combine
Theme preference is stored beside the layout; both change without touching recipes, Undo or the library.
Adapt
Each size class is recovered against the current window, so a layout saved on a large monitor opens safely on a laptop.
Driven by
authoring.dispatch({kind:'tabs.arrange', tab, layout}), recoverDockLayout, parseTree, recoverWindows.

Live dock

Implemented

Scripts are required for the live dock.

What
The production DockView with sample panels: drag tabs and tab bars, float, attach, split, resize, close and reopen from the ⋯ menus. Its layout is not saved.
When
Try interactions here before changing dock-view.ts; the Studio uses the same class with real panels.
Combine
Menus, drags and splitters behave exactly as in the Studio.
Adapt
Fixed-size demo area.
Driven by
DockView from src/studio-ui/dock/dock-view.ts with sample panels.
04

Components

Components are presentation only. Each one names the application action or read-only state behind it, and shows the application's reason when it is unavailable. Nothing here owns validation, Undo, persistence or export decisions.

Buttons

Implemented
Choose your Cyberpunk 2077 folder in Settings › Game first.
What
Primary (yellow, one per region: the commitment), default, quiet (secondary in a region), ghost (tool clusters), danger (destructive where Undo is not enough) and small/icon-only variants. Toggle tools use aria-pressed; a quiet button that holds a state (Poses: Stand still, Idle) shows it pressed in cyan (text, fill and edge), so no status line need repeat it.
When
Primary marks the action that records or produces something (Save version, Build). Never two primaries side by side.
Combine
Icon + verb label. Icon-only buttons are allowed in tool clusters and row trailing actions, always with an accessible name and tooltip.
Adapt
Header actions collapse to icon-only buttons below 1100 px; panel buttons wrap onto new rows rather than shrinking.
Driven by
Availability = the action's capability. An unavailable main action keeps its place and its focus, and states the application's reason (the command palette and menus show the same text); an unavailable primary drops its yellow and fades like a default button, so it never reads as the thing to press (C-25).
Keyboard & access
The menu pattern (UI-84): an unavailable button is aria-disabled, not disabled, so keyboard, touch and screen-reader users reach it. Its reason is its accessible description and appears as a tip on focus, hover or tap; a click runs nothing. Native disabled stays for form fields.

Link buttons

Implemented
  • You have the newest version, 0.9.0.
  • Every XF Studio version, with what changed in each.
  • You have the newest version, 0.9.0.
  • Every XF Studio version, with what changed in each.
What
A command written as underlined accent text (.link-button): Help's rows, a setup card's licence link, the Save Explorer's references. Unavailable, it turns body-text colour, loses its underline and shows the not-allowed cursor; its label says what is happening (Checking for updates…) and its reason is its description, as for a button.
When
An action that reads as part of a list or sentence, or opens something to read. Anything that records or produces something is a button.
Combine
One per row, with a muted line under it saying what it does or what it last found; the line keeps its text while the link is busy, so nothing below moves.
Adapt
The label wraps with its row at a narrow panel rather than truncating; the line under it keeps its place while the label changes.
Driven by
Availability is the action's capability (applyCapability), as for a button: an unavailable link stays in place and focusable.
Keyboard & access
Native button with aria-disabled while unavailable, so keyboard and screen-reader users still reach it and hear why; a click runs nothing. The unavailable state isn't colour alone: the underline goes and the label names the state. It turns body-text colour (--text): no accent and no underline, so it reads as a label, not a link, and it stays above the muted line under it.
Avoid
Fading a link button with opacity (it drops below readable contrast); a disabled link that keeps its underline and accent colour, so it still looks live.

Chips, badges and status vocabulary

Implemented
No version yetSavedChanged since last versionNewer version savedWorking…Version 3
Can be builtExperimentalPreview only
CurrentStale — changed sinceBlockedOpen now
Early accessSoon
StudioBetathe product's release stage: the header only
What
Chips describe document/library state; badges qualify a result or capability. The words are fixed vocabulary. The library chip, which compares the collection with the last version saved (its work is always in the library): No version yet, Saved, Changed since last version, Newer version saved, Working… while the library is busy (or reading the last version back to compare with, only while that read runs), Version N (neutral) when that version couldn't be read back, so nothing can be compared (its tooltip says so; it is read again on the next library refresh), and Read-only (neutral) in a window that doesn't hold its workspace (t-read-only-window). A finish's export status, as a finish group's heading or a badge: Can be built, Experimental, Preview only. A result's state: Current, Stale, Blocked. One more badge says library state: Open now, on the Library's row of the collection open now (with that row's signal background and no Open button: it is already open), and nowhere else. A finished Build states its limits in one plain sentence (built and checked, not tested in game, nothing installed) rather than in badges. A part of the Studio that isn't finished carries the Early access stage tag (Component library › Stage tag), never a badge. Soon marks a planned entry and shows only with research tools on. The product's own release stage is one marker, Beta, in exactly one place: beside the product name in the header, as the accent badge (its tooltip says what the beta means and where to report a problem). It is the release channel's word, never a module's or a result's, and appears nowhere else (UI-160).
When
Whenever a result could be mistaken for more than it is. A green badge never implies game rendering.
Combine
The library chip sits beside the preset name in the header, the one place it shows; result badges sit in the result card's head; a finish's export status is its group heading in the finish chooser.
Adapt
Below 720 px the header hides the chip; the Library panel's sentence still says whether your work is saved.
Driven by
libraryState() from library.summary(); result badges from files.snapshot().package.
Avoid
Colour-only status dots without words; vague labels like “OK” or “Done”; words outside this vocabulary (“Autosaved draft”: work always saves itself, so the chip only ever compares with the last version).

Text, title and select fields

Implemented
What
Sunken inputs with a strong boundary. Names commit on Enter or blur and revert on Escape; the application validates (e.g. 1–120 characters) and a refused rename restores the previous name with a toast.
When
Inline rename in rows (F2 / double-click), the collection title in Presets, value popovers and selects for enumerations with few choices.
Combine
A field is always paired with a visible label or an accessible name; inline rename replaces the row's button in place.
Adapt
Fields fill their column; titles truncate with an ellipsis rather than wrapping.
Driven by
collection.rename, preset.edit rename, layer.edit rename; application validation decides.
Keyboard & access
Native text inputs keep the browser's text context menu; Studio suppresses native menus only on non-text surfaces.

Slider with readout (one Undo per drag)

Implemented
Turn on Smooth point gradients to adjust blending.
What
Range input with a monospaced readout. Pointer down or arrow keys begin a control transaction, every value is an edit, release/blur commits one Undo step, and Escape restores the starting value.
When
Continuous recipe values (opacity, pigment, softness, reach, flake settings) and view preferences (FOV, exposure).
Combine
Pair related sliders in one row only when both fit (Colour + Opacity); disabled sliders keep their reason directly beneath.
Adapt
Sliders fill their column; readouts never wrap.
Driven by
authoring.controlBegin(id, layerId) → controlEdit(id, action) → controlCommit(id) / controlCancel(id). Ranges come from actionDescriptors() limits, not UI constants.
Keyboard & access
The label is the input's label. A control's note line never moves the layout (UI-90): once a control has a note it keeps the line (an empty note keeps its height, a disabled reason takes its place); a control without one says why it is disabled in its tooltip and description, and its panel says it once.

Expanders (one disclosure for every level)

Implemented

What
One expander folds everything that folds: the parts of V (group), their sections, a section's subsections, rows and the author groups inside a row. Every level has the same chevron (10 px, pointing right when folded and down when open, turning without moving anything), the same gap between chevron and text, and the same hover and focus. Only the type steps down, in one hierarchy: group (display face, uppercase, the largest) › section (display, uppercase) › subsection (display, uppercase, muted, one step in) › row (UI face, sentence case: content, not a heading) › author group (UI face, sentence case, the smallest, with its count). A section with rows has Expand all / Collapse all at the far right of its heading, after its show/hide switch; its icon and name say what a press does now. A folded heading holding search matches shows how many.
When
Any foldable hierarchy: the Character panel now; later feature panels with grouped rows. Never build a second chevron style.
Combine
A heading row is: expander, help tip (when it has one), then at the far right its switch and Expand all. Author groups with a single choice in the row share one Other mods group, last, sorted by label; each choice's mod is in its tooltip.
Adapt
Labels truncate to one line; the switch and Expand all never wrap below the heading.
Driven by
Presentation state: every fold (a group's, a section's, a row's and an author group's) is remembered across reloads in the workspace's view state (lib-view-state: the expanded.set {keys, expanded} UI preference, never Undo, not part of a layout); a row whose mod isn't loaded keeps its state until it shows. Expand all opens the section's rows and unfolds their author groups; the palette offers it per section and folds or opens every section.
Keyboard & access
The WAI disclosure pattern: a button with aria-expanded and aria-controls, inside the heading element of its level (h3–h5), so headings keep their outline. Enter or Space folds; an author-group heading also folds with Left and unfolds with Right from inside its listbox. Expand all is an icon button named for what it will do.

Help tips (what something is)

Implemented

Files

A save is read on this computer and never changed or uploaded.

What
A small help icon beside a heading, row or control holds what it is or does (hair physics is not simulated; a row follows a switcher; what a save import touches) in a rich tooltip: an optional bold title and short paragraphs. Inline text is kept for what the person can act on: a status with Try again, a choice to make, why something failed. One tip for the page floats above everything, so showing it never moves the layout.
When
Every panel, instead of an informational note under a heading or control. A control's help and a section's { title, help } produce it.
Combine
Beside the label, outside it (pressing the icon never works the control). An empty help keeps the icon's place hidden, so a row's layout doesn't jump when its shown option has nothing to say.
Adapt
The tip is at most 300 px wide and stays inside the window, below the icon or above it near the bottom.
Driven by
Static or read-only text only; setHelp(icon, text) changes it in place (the Body switch's help follows the uncensored setting).
Keyboard & access
The icon is a button in the tab order named “About ”; its text is the button's accessible description, read on focus without opening anything. The tip shows on focus or hover and pins open on a click or tap; Escape, a second click or leaving closes it. It never takes focus and holds no controls.

Creator options (generated rows)

Implemented
Updating…

Not prepared yet · Preparing

What
Every creator option of the shown V, generated from the installed game and mods, in one hierarchy: the parts of V (Head, Body, Clothing), then the panel's own sections (Head: Skin; Face with Eyes, Eyebrows, Eyelashes, Nose, Mouth & lips, Ears, Jaw & shape, Makeup, Piercings and Face details inside; Hair; Teeth; Other), where each row lands by what it controls (the preview detail its slot feeds, then the words of its slot, option names and link keys, then the category the game or mod declared), never by display name or a per-mod table, then rows of options sharing a creator slot (the active one shows), and the active option's choices opened in place, as a swatch grid for colours and chips otherwise, Off first. Every colour choice, the game's or a mod's, is a narrow swatch: the game's icon (unless a mod replaced that colour's resource), else the colour derived from the resource that wins for it (a hair, brow or lash profile as a small root-to-tip gradient), else the definition's colour. A tightly clustered set of derived colours (one maker's group, or the row) is shown spread apart in lightness and hue, in order; the row's own chip keeps the true colour, and a contrast help tip (a half-filled circle) beside the row's help tip says the list shows more contrast. Resting on a swatch, or focusing it, shows the swatch card (lib-swatch-card): its true colour, name and maker. What the 3D view shows is part of the same hierarchy: each section has at most one show/hide switch, on its heading, for what it draws; why it can't change is the reason tip, and what it shows is the heading's help tip. Everything folds with the shared expander (c-expanders); what a row or heading is lives in help tips (c-help-tips), never an inline line. A changed row is marked and offers Reset to the V's own; an option with an Off choice offers Off; a row whose choice the 3D view doesn't draw, or draws only in part, shows a fixed-size marker; the row's label dims only when nothing of it is drawn. The search finds options and choices on the host, over every choice. An open row's choices are prepared ahead in the background, the ones in view first: a choice not prepared yet carries a small hollow corner mark, the one being prepared a turning cyan mark, one that couldn't be prepared ahead a filled warning mark, and a ready one none. One short line under the search names the marks; what they mean is its help tip.
When
The Character panel. The prominent action, Hide my V's own makeup, and Reset all sit above the rows; everything else is per row.
Combine
One status line of fixed height above (never moves the layout): Updating… (for a choice that wasn't prepared ahead, why it takes a few seconds the first time), what failed, or the first of the plain lines about what couldn't be used, clamped to one line; Try again, Keep my changes and Details keep their place when not offered. Undo and Redo sit beside the V's source and step this V's own changes (creator options and Clothing), as Ctrl+Z does anywhere in the panel; the header's Undo and History follow what you last edited (a preset or a V, t-undo), so after a Character edit they step the V too, and say so.
Adapt
Single column at every width; row values and the status line truncate, never wrap; the swatch grid fills the row with as many columns as fit.
Driven by
character.setOption (with a switcher choice's activated options), character.setOwnMakeup (the V's own makeup, a switch), character.reset, character.resetAll, character.keepChanges, character.retry, history.undo/redo naming the V's scope (character:<id>); authoring.characterPanel(), characterView(), characterChoices(option, want, query) and characterSearch(query) (frozen, paged), characterPrefetch(option, positions, focus) and characterStopPrefetch(option) (each choice's prepared-ahead state, polled per row), characterSwatches(option) (a colour row's derived swatches and icons), a row's choices grouped by maker under folding headings when they come from more than one (the projection's groups and modGroups), heading switches from characterPanelTree contributions (preview.setDetail/setHair/setPiercings/setBody, character.setClothing), preview.setUncensored in Body, character.clearPreparedFiles under Files, coverage notes from the preview's projection.
Keyboard & access
Rows are buttons with aria-expanded and an accessible description (where the option comes from, the V's own choice, whether the 3D view draws it). The marker is decoration; the row's description says whether its choice is not shown or not fully shown. Choices are a listbox: arrow keys, Home and End move focus without choosing (each choice prepares the V anew), Enter or Space chooses; the chosen one is aria-selected by identity, and each choice's origin is its accessible description. Choosing keeps focus on the same item. A choice's prepared-ahead state joins its accessible description and tooltip ("not prepared yet", "being prepared"); the marks are decoration (aria-hidden in the legend), sit in the item's corner so they never move the layout, keep their own fill to stay legible over any swatch in both themes, and stop turning under reduced motion. Hovering or focusing a choice prepares it next. Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y inside the panel step the character's own history. A heading switch is named for what it shows ("Show hair in the 3D view"); when it can't change it stays focusable with aria-disabled, and its reason is its description and the page's reason tip.

Switch

Implemented
Saved hair preview is unavailable.
What
Binary settings that apply immediately. Recipe switches are one Undo step; preview switches are workspace preferences with no Undo.

On/off state. Use a button when the effect is an action (Try again) rather than a state.

Switches stack in a section with their notes; a switch that unlocks a slider sits directly above it (Smooth point gradients → Point blend).

Full-width rows in every size class.
Driven by
Recipe switches: control transactions (pigment/softness) or dispatch (layer.setSymmetry); preview switches: preview.* actions.

Native checkbox with role=switch; the disabled reason is visible text, not only a tooltip.

A labelled group of toggle buttons with aria-pressed; a disabled group states its reason in the note line and as the group's description.
