Keyboard & access
Not a live region (it changes with every hover); the same bindings are in each viewport's accessible name and the Keyboard & mouse dialog. Both strips use the theme-aware --stage-* tokens. Custom cursors are white glyphs with a dark halo and fall back to grab / nwse-resize keywords; blur or a hidden page clears held modifiers. Reduced motion removes the tooltip fade.

Selection and editing handles

Implemented
What
Drawn by the UV and on-head editor adapters, not the dock: contour points (selected is larger and white), gold tangent diamonds (guides that may cross the eye opening), warp origin circle, pull square and dashed reach ring. Guides show the contour before warp; the painted makeup shows the result after warp.
When
Drag to edit (one Undo per gesture), Shift-drag to rotate, Shift+wheel to scale, double-click the outline to insert, Escape to cancel. Shift always means a shape tool: off makeup it does nothing. Right-drag (or Ctrl-drag) pans and wheel zooms — view changes are never edits.
Combine
Selecting a handle updates the Shape, Pigment & edge and Warp inspectors.
Adapt
Handle sizes are fixed in screen pixels; zoom the UV map or the camera for precision.
Driven by
Opaque gesture sessions (beginGesture/applyGesture/endGesture) inside the device adapters; the presentation only hosts them.

Guidance callout

Implemented
Getting started · 1 of 8

Looks are made of layers

Each layer is one shape of makeup with its own colour and finish. Layers stack like real makeup: the top of the list sits in front.

Start by adding a layer, or use one that's already there.

What
A non-modal card with an eyebrow (tour and step), a title, a content area rendered from markdown-lite help text (bold, bullets and key chips generated from the binding catalogue), an optional note, progress marks and a row of custom buttons. Command buttons dispatch ordinary typed actions (“Do it for me”); Back, Next and Done move through the tour.
When
Tour steps and the one-time onboarding offer. Never for errors or confirmations: those stay toasts and menus.
Combine
Sits beside the spotlighted anchor, or centred when a step has none. The onboarding offer uses the same card in the lower-left corner without a scrim, away from toasts (lower right) and the 3D view setup card (docked in the 3D view, or floating only when that view isn't shown), and follows that card rather than showing beside it.
Adapt
360 px wide, capped to the window; below 560 px it becomes a sheet above or below the target. Its height follows its content and it scrolls if the window is short.
Driven by
GuidanceService snapshot (guidance.startTour, next, back, skip, finish) in src/studio-ui/guidance/engine.ts; button capabilities from the same port capabilities as every control.
Keyboard & access
role=dialog, aria-modal=false, labelled by its title and described by its body. Focus moves to the title when a person navigates, never when a step advances by itself; every step is announced. Esc skips, → and Enter go on, ← goes back; Enter on a button presses it. An unavailable button's reason is written in the note, not only in a tooltip.
Avoid
Anchoring to CSS selectors, text the reader has to decode (IDs, action names), or buttons that change the look without going through validation and Undo.

Spotlight

Implemented
What
One rectangle around the anchor whose outer shadow dims the rest of the UI in the dark theme and lightens it in the light theme (the --guidance-scrim token), with a ring in --guidance-ring. With no anchor the whole window is dimmed and the callout is centred.
When
While a tour step points at something. It is never used to block input: the dimmed UI stays usable, so a step can ask the person to try the control.
Combine
Lights an anchor (layers.add, uv.canvas, header.package …); if the control is hidden but its panel is showing, it lights the panel; if the panel is closed or behind a tab, the callout offers to show it through the ordinary panel command instead.
Adapt
Follows the anchor's rectangle every frame while a tour runs, cut to what its scrolling panel shows, so window resizing, docking, floating and scrolling keep it aligned. It is a fixed overlay and never takes layout space.
Driven by
AnchorRegistry (src/studio-ui/guidance/anchors.ts): panels register named anchors as they build their controls; placeCallout() in placement.ts.

Help view

Implemented
What
A dock panel with one search over guided tours, questions and answers, and the keyboard and mouse reference, plus links to the public knowledge pages, the issue tracker and this Interface guide (it opens in a new tab: the localhost Studio's own copy, or the published guide from the desktop app; Back to XF Studio closes the tab opened by localhost, returning to the same workspace; elsewhere the link reads XF Studio site).
When
F1, the header's Help button or the command palette. 3 tours today: Getting started, Your V, camera and settings, What's new in the beta.
Combine
Opens beside the inspectors (closed by default). Tours start from here; a tour you finished or skipped says so (Done, Skipped), and one not started carries no badge. The reference is the same catalogue as the Keyboard & mouse sheet.
Adapt
A panel like any other: dock, float or tab it. Tour rows drop their status badge below 420 px.
Driven by
HELP_TOPICS and HELP_LINKS (data), helpReference() over bindingReference(), port.links.open() for named public pages (the host opens them; the view never sends a URL).
05

Component library

Every component panels and features compose, with its full contract: purpose, anatomy, variants, states, sizes, how it adapts, keyboard and access, do and avoid, and a composition example. Import from src/studio-ui/components. Each specimen is built live by the production component.

Component-first UI

Rule
What
All UI is composed from this library. Panels and feature views compose components and wire them to actions and snapshots; they do not build controls (buttons, fields, lists, tabs, dialogs, progress) from raw elements. Components that only one feature needs still live in the library, in the Feature-specific category.
When
A feature that needs a control the library lacks specifies it (behaviour, states, accessibility) and the UI component track builds or extends it here, with its entry on this page. tests/ui-component-ratchet.test.ts counts the ad hoc controls left outside the library per file: no file may gain one, and each count only goes down.
Categories
General: Button, Button label and weight in place, Icon button, Switch, Slider, Slider with value, Pair control, Bipolar slider, Scrub slider, Segmented control, Choice list, Choice preview, Choice layouts, Colour field, Select field, Combobox, Search field, Expander, Group section, Help tip, Reason tip, Menu, value and confirm popovers, Stage tag, Ordered list, Menu row with secondary action, Choice popover, Tab strip, Panel header, Badge, note, empty state and progress, Tree view, Size bar, Remembered view state, Folder setting, Record list, Conflict notice, Workspace notice
Layout: Layout primitives, Split view, Splitter
Feature-specific: Light list, Direction dial, 3D view at rest (not drawn), Mod line, Swatch card

Button

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A command with a verb label and an optional icon: the default control for doing something.
Module
studio-ui/controls.ts · button, applyCapability · General
Anatomy
Bevelled box · optional leading icon · label (a span) · nothing else. Icon-only drops the label and keeps it as the accessible name and tooltip.
Variants
default, primary (one per region), quiet, ghost (tool clusters), danger; small; iconOnly; menu (opens a menu: aria-haspopup).
States
rest, hover, active, focus-visible, pressed (aria-pressed for a tool toggle), unavailable (the main-action pattern: aria-disabled with its reason).
Sizes
28 px (--control-h), small 24 px (--control-h-sm); icon-only is square.
When
Any action in panel content, headers, sheets and toasts.
Combine
A row of actions: h("div", { class: "row wrap gap-s" }, button({ label: "Check", icon: "check", onClick }), button({ label: "Build", variant: "primary", onClick })). A toast's actions and a sheet's footer are buttons too.
Adapt
Labels never wrap; a crowded header shows icon-only buttons with the label as tooltip and name.
Driven by
Availability is the action's capability: applyCapability(control, capability).
Keyboard & access
Native button; Enter and Space. An unavailable one stays focusable, says why (its description and the page's reason tip) and runs nothing when pressed.
Do
Start the label with a verb; use one primary per region; mark menu triggers with menu.
Avoid
Building h("button", { class: "btn" }) by hand (it skips the unavailable guard); native disabled on a main action; two primaries side by side.
See also
c-buttons

Button label and weight in place

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
Changes a button's words or weight after it is built, without replacing it: a busy label (Check now → Checking…), a label that follows state (Show them / Hide them), or the region's main action moving to another button (a newer version makes Open the releases page primary and Check now quiet).
Module
studio-ui/controls.ts · setButtonLabel, setButtonVariant · General
Anatomy
The same button: its icon, focus, handlers and place stay; only the label span or the variant class changes.
Variants
setButtonLabel(button, text); setButtonVariant(button, "primary" | "quiet" | "danger" | "ghost" | undefined) (undefined is the default button). An icon-only button's label is its accessible name, and its tip too when the tip was the label.
States
Busy: the label says what is happening, ending in an ellipsis, and the button is unavailable (applyCapability) until the answer arrives; the result line beside it keeps its last text, so the row doesn't reflow. Exactly one variant at a time.
Sizes
As Button. A busy label should be no longer than the rest label where it can be, so the row doesn't jump.
When
A button whose words or weight follow state. Build a new button only when the action itself changes.
Combine
Settings › Updates: setButtonLabel(checkNow, checking ? "Checking…" : "Check now"), then setButtonVariant(releases, newer ? "primary" : "quiet").
Adapt
Nothing extra: the label and weight change in place at every width.
Driven by
The feature's snapshot, on each update; both calls change nothing when the value is already right, so calling them every frame costs nothing.
Keyboard & access
The button keeps focus while its label changes; a busy button is aria-disabled with its reason, so a second press runs nothing and a screen reader hears why. A label change on a focused button is announced by the result line (role="status"), not by the button.
Do
Pair a busy label with the unavailable state; keep one primary per region when moving the weight.
Avoid
Editing the button's inner span or toggling primary/quiet classes by hand (tests/ui-component-ratchet.test.ts refuses it); rebuilding the button to change its words (focus is lost).
See also
c-buttons

Icon button

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A borderless square button for a surface's chrome: panel header actions, a sheet's or toast's close, a row's visibility or more-actions mark.
Module
studio-ui/components/icon-button.ts · iconButton · General
Anatomy
24 px square (22 px small) · one 16 px icon · no border until hover.
Variants
small; menu (aria-haspopup); pressed (a toggle, coloured signal when on); mode (with pressed: a mode such as mirrored sides, tinted as well when on, so it reads at a glance); expanded (a disclosure); className for placement hooks.
States
rest (muted), hover, focus-visible, pressed, unavailable (the main-action pattern, faded).
Sizes
24 px; small 22 px. It never shrinks inside a header (the panel header keeps its actions whole).
When
Chrome around content. Inside panel content, among bordered buttons, use button({ iconOnly }) so it matches them.
Combine
A sheet's head: h("div", { class: "sheet-head" }, h("h2", {}, title), iconButton({ label: "Close", icon: "close", onClick: close })).
Adapt
Fixed size at every width.
Driven by
The owner's intent (close, open a menu, toggle); availability via applyCapability.
Keyboard & access
Named by label, titled by it too unless title says more; menu triggers announce their popup; toggles announce their state.
Do
Give every icon button a label that names the action and its object ("Hide Petal wash"). Use mode for a mode the person turns on for a region, not for per-row marks that are on by default.
Avoid
Hand-built .icon-btn elements; an icon button without a tooltip.
See also
d-group

Switch

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
An on/off setting that takes effect at once.
Module
studio-ui/controls.ts · Toggle · General
Anatomy
Track and thumb · label to its right · optional help tip beside it · reserved note line when it can carry a reason.
Variants
with or without help; reserveNote.
States
off, on, focus-visible, disabled (a form field: native disabled with its reason on the note line or in the tooltip).; mixed (update(false, { mixed: true }): a switch over several things of which some are on shows a dash across its track instead of a thumb, never a half-slid thumb, says so in its label (mixedLabel, "Symmetric · some regions") and reads "mixed", announced as a checkbox since ARIA's switch has no mixed value; a press turns it fully on)
Sizes
30 × 16 px track; row height 24 px.
When
Settings and visibility toggles that apply immediately (Show my V's own makeup).
Combine
Stack switches in a section; one per line.
Adapt
The label wraps; the track stays at its start.
Driven by
An application action on change; its state from a read-only snapshot.
Keyboard & access
input type=checkbox role=switch with a label; Space toggles; the reason is its description.
Do
Name the setting, not the action ("Show my V's own makeup").
Avoid
Raw checkboxes; a switch that needs a Save button.
See also
c-switch

Slider

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A continuous value with a live readout; one Undo step per drag or keyboard burst.
Module
studio-ui/controls.ts · Slider, bindRangeTransaction, fillRange, NoteLine · General
Anatomy
Label (with help tip) and readout on one line · range track with its signal fill · reserved note line.
Variants
reserveNote for a limit that comes and goes; help.
States
rest, dragging (a transaction is open), cancelled (Escape restores the start), disabled with its reason.
Sizes
Full width of its column; track 4 px, thumb 12 × 16 px.
When
Values judged by eye (opacity, softness).
Combine
Beside a colour field in a two-column form row; under a section title.
Adapt
Full width; the readout stays right-aligned.
Driven by
A begin/edit/commit/cancel transaction the application groups into one Undo step. relabel(label, accessibleLabel?) renames the same value everywhere it is said (the visible label, the range's name, the help tip) when its meaning follows a mode: Shimmer's "Sparkle density" and Glitter's "Flake density", "Edge softness" and "Selected point softness". Owners never rewrite a label through the DOM.
Keyboard & access
Labelled range; arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End; Escape during a drag restores the starting value.
Do
Format the readout in the person's terms ("85%").
Avoid
A number box beside a plain slider: use Slider with value.
See also
c-slider

Slider with value

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A slider whose one readout is also where its exact value is typed, with an optional reset: one readout per value, never a second number box.
Module
studio-ui/components/slider-with-value.ts · SliderWithValue · General
Anatomy
Label (with help tip) · the readout (typed into in place) · reset, shown only while the value is set · range under them · a note line only when asked for. Inline: a short label, the range, the readout and reset on one line (a pair's sides).
Variants
reset with defaultValue; inline with accessibleLabel; reserveNote; quietReason (a reason that is information, such as a dependency on the switch above, keeps the muted note tone, never the warning tone: Expression › Transitions' Duration, UI-145); ends (the two ends' words small under the track, as the Bipolar and Scrub sliders: "Crisp … Game-like"); update(value, { text }) for a readout the owner words itself (a pair's "14 / 10 %", shown muted).
States
default; set (away from its default: the label emphasised with a signal mark, the reset shown); dragging; typing an exact value; the owner's readout; disabled (its reason on the note line when reserved, else in the tooltip and description).
Sizes
Label line 22 px; track as Slider; about 44 px a control stacked, 22 px inline, so a list of them stays dense at 300 px.
When
Values people also type, with a meaningful default (expression and shape values).
Combine
Rows of them inside a Group section; two inline ones make a Pair control's separate state. A list of them shares one disabled reason, said once by the panel.
Adapt
Full width; the label truncates with an ellipsis before the readout or reset would move.
Driven by
The Slider's transaction for drags; a typed value, Delete or the reset is one begin/edit/commit step, clamped and snapped to the step. relabel(label, accessibleLabel?) renames the same value everywhere it is said (the visible label, the range's name, the help tip, the typed field and the reset) when its meaning follows a mode: Shimmer's "Sparkle density" and Glitter's "Flake density", "Edge softness" and "Selected point softness". Owners never rewrite a label through the DOM.
Keyboard & access
The range is labelled by the visible label (or accessibleLabel) and speaks the formatted value; one tab stop: Enter types an exact value in the readout's place (Enter commits, Escape reverts, focus returns to the range), Delete or Backspace returns to the default; the field is named "<label>, exact value"; the reset is "Reset <label>".
Do
Give it the default so people can see what they changed.
Avoid
A number box beside the slider; a reserved note line under every row of a list; a faded reset on every row.

Pair control

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A left/right pair of values (a brow's two sides, two eyelids), edited together or apart. Whether it is linked is the owner's state, decided in a group heading's mirror toggle or a whole-panel switch, never by a toggle on every pair.
Module
studio-ui/components/pair-control.ts · PairControl · General
Anatomy
Linked: one Slider with value under the pair's name. Separate: the pair's name, then one inline line per side ("L", "R": range, readout, reset).
Variants
side labels and names (sideLabels, sideNames); every Slider with value option.
States
linked; uneven (linked while the sides differ: the one readout says both values, muted, "14 / 10 %", and the next edit sets both); separate; disabled.
Sizes
Linked about 44 px; separate about 70 px.
When
Symmetric features edited together by default (brows, lids).
Combine
Inside a Group section whose heading holds the region's mirror toggle (an icon button with mode).
Adapt
Rows stack vertically at every width.
Driven by
Edits carry { sides: "both" | "left" | "right", value }; update(values, { linked, disabled, reason }).
Keyboard & access
Linked, the range is named "<label>, both sides"; separate, the sides are a group named by the pair with ranges named "<label>, left" and "<label>, right".
Do
Default to linked; show uneven sides in the readout, not a note.
Avoid
Repeating the pair's name in its row ("Brow height" over "Brow height, both sides"); a link toggle or pill under every pair.

Bipolar slider

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
One value between two opposite directions with a resting centre, for a movement that goes one way or the other but never both (look left or right, brow up or down).
Module
studio-ui/components/bipolar-slider.ts · BipolarSlider · General
Anatomy
Label (with help tip) and one readout that names the direction ("0", "20 % right") · reset, shown only away from the centre · range with a centre mark, filled from the centre to the thumb · the two direction words, small, at the track's ends · note line only on request.
Variants
unit; format for other readouts; detent; reset: false; reserveNote; asymmetric ranges (the centre mark sits at 0 wherever that falls).
States
at the centre; set (away from it: the label emphasised with a signal mark); mixed (the data sets both directions: the readout says Mixed, the thumb has a dashed edge at the net value, nothing changes until the next edit replaces both with one value); dragging; typing an exact value; disabled with its reason.
Sizes
Label line 22 px; track as Slider; direction words --fs-2xs. About 50 px a control, so a list of them stays dense at 300 px.
When
Opposing controls merged into one value (gaze sideways and up/down, brow up/down, jaw left/right). A value that only grows from zero is a Slider with value.
Combine
Rows inside a Group section, like Slider with value: new BipolarSlider({ label: "Look sideways", min: -100, max: 100, step: 1, unit: "%", ends: { negative: "Left", positive: "Right" }, transaction }). Name the axis in the label and the directions at the ends; never put both directions in the label.
Adapt
Full width; the label truncates with an ellipsis before the readout or reset would move; the direction words stay at the ends.
Driven by
The Slider's begin/edit/commit/cancel transaction for drags and keys; a typed value, Delete, a double-click or the reset is one begin/edit/commit step, clamped and snapped. update(value, { mixed, disabled, reason }) from the owner's snapshot.
Keyboard & access
A native range labelled by the visible label; its value text is the readout's words ("20 % right", "Mixed: 20 % right"); the direction words are decoration. One tab stop: Enter types an exact value in the readout's place (Enter commits, Escape reverts, focus returns to the slider), Delete or Backspace returns to the centre, arrows and Home/End as any range; the reset is "Reset <label>".
Do
Snap to the centre on a drag so rest is easy to hit; show which way in words, not only by position.
Avoid
Two sliders for directions that can't both happen ("Look in" and "Look out"); a signed number without its direction word.
See also
lib-slider-value

Light list

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A lighting setup's lights as an ordered list, one compact row each, for choosing the light the editor below shows.
Module
studio-ui/components/light-list.ts · LightList · Feature-specific
Anatomy
The Ordered list's row (grip · lead · name and meta · trailing) with a colour chip (the layer swatch) and a glyph for the light's kind (a sun for directional, the lighting mark for spot) in the lead, the light's name, and one muted line of what matters at a glance ("40 · shadows": strength and shadows; the glyph shows the kind).
Variants
None beyond the Ordered list's; the kind glyph follows the light.
States
rest, hover, selected (signal fill with the inset edge), dragging, renaming in place, disabled (the whole list, with the editor's reason).
Sizes
Rows 32 px (--row-h); chip 16 px; the meta line hides below 250 px of container width.
When
The lights of the shown lighting setup in Camera & light. Other ordered collections use the Ordered list itself.
Combine
Above the light editor, with an Add light button under it: new LightList({ label: "Lights", onSelect, onMove, onRename, onDelete, onDuplicate, onMenu, maxLength: 60 }); the owner keeps the selection and passes it to update(items, selected).
Adapt
Full width; names truncate before the chip or grip would move; the meta line goes first when narrow.
Driven by
Intents only (select, move, rename, delete, duplicate, menu); the owner dispatches the setup actions and feeds rows from the setup's read model.
Keyboard & access
The Ordered list's keyboard: arrows move focus, Alt+Up/Down reorder, F2 renames, Delete removes, the menu key opens the row menu. Each row is named "<name>, <kind> light, <meta>", so the chip and glyph never carry meaning alone.
Do
Keep the meta line short and parallel across rows (strength, shadows): the name has priority and the meta gives way first.
Avoid
A colour or glyph as the only way to tell lights apart; hand-built rows.
See also
lib-item-list, lib-direction-dial

Direction dial

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
Where a light sits around V, seen from above: one handle whose angle round the dial is the light's direction and whose distance from the centre is its height, with a height scale beside it that says the height as a number.
Module
studio-ui/components/direction-dial.ts · DirectionDial, dialPoint, dialDirection, dragDirection, snapStep, heightTicks, heightY, fitDialSize, azimuthWords, DIAL_MIN_SIZE, DIAL_DEFAULT_SIZE, ANGLE_SNAP · Feature-specific
Anatomy
Label line with two readouts (the angle, the height), each typed into in place · a round dial: V's head at the centre with her nose toward the bottom edge ("Front"), "Behind" at the top, "V's right" upright on the left and "V's left" on the right as when you face her, a dashed ring for level with the head, the edge for straight below · the handle in the light's colour · the setup's other lights as small dots · a vertical height scale on the right (+89° to −89°, labelled ticks at the ends, the quarters and level; the current height marked with a pointer and its value in the light's colour) · while dragging, a dashed radius from the centre to the edge through the handle, the other dots dimmed · a resize bar under the dial · note line only on request.
Variants
elevation range (default −89° to 89°); reserveNote; others dots on or off; onResize to keep the chosen size.
States
rest; dragging (the radius line shows, the other dots dim; Shift keeps the angle, Alt snaps the angle around V to 15°, Shift and Alt together keep the height; Escape restores the start); keyboard burst (the same radius and dimming); typing an exact angle or height; resizing (the bar's grip lit); focus-visible (the dial's ring, the bar's ring); unavailable with its reason on the note line.
Sizes
The drawing is 180 px wide at least and 280 px by default; the resize bar sets it (kept as the controlSize.set UI preference under lighting-direction), clamped to the control's width, and drawn smaller while the panel is narrower (fitDialSize). The resize bar is the library's Size bar under the drawing (it sets the drawing's height and reports its width; Delete, Backspace or a double-click go back to the default, Escape during a drag goes back to where it started), 12 px tall. Only the drawing scales: its words and ticks stay --fs-2xs and the current height --fs-xs mono at every size (counter-scaled by --dial-unit).
When
A light's direction in the lighting setup editor. A single angle alone is a Slider with value.
Combine
Under the Light list's selected light, above its distance and strength: new DirectionDial({ label: "Direction", transaction, onResize: (size, final) => final && keep(size) }), then update({ azimuth, elevation }, { colour, others, size }).
Adapt
Keeps its aspect; the chosen size shrinks to the control's width when the panel narrows and returns when it widens; centred; the readouts stay on the label line; the layout below moves only by the dial's own size.
Driven by
A begin/edit/commit/cancel transaction of { azimuth, elevation } in degrees: a drag or a keyboard burst is one transaction, a typed value one step. onResize(size, final) reports the chosen width; the owner keeps it on release. The owner turns the direction into the light's placement about the head.
Keyboard & access
The dial is one tab stop, role=slider with the angle as its value and "330°, from the front, V's left, 20° up" as its value text. Left and Right turn by 5°, Page Up and Page Down by 15°, Up and Down raise and lower by 5° (Alt: to the next 15° step), Home brings it to the front, Enter types the angle. The readouts are named "<label> angle, exact value" and "<label> height, exact value". The resize bar is its own tab stop, role=separator named "Resize <label>" with the width as its value: Up and Down shrink and enlarge by 16 px, Home and End go to the smallest and largest; a double-click on it returns to the default size. Its tooltip is the Size bar's ("Drag to resize · double-click to reset").
Do
Show the light's own colour on the handle and the height marker and its neighbours as dots, so the rig reads at a glance.
Avoid
Raw x, y, z fields for a light's position; two unrelated sliders for angle and height; a height scale without the current value marked.
See also
lib-light-list, lib-slider-value

Scrub slider

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A spring-loaded slider for an operation on many values at once (Adjust all › Intensity): it rests at the middle, previews live while moved, applies on release as one step and springs back.
Module
studio-ui/components/scrub-slider.ts · ScrubSlider, SCRUB_REST · General
Anatomy
Label (with help tip) · curves (optional: a frameless icon-only Segmented, one segment per easing, chosen and focused as the standalone Curve strip is) · readout (the position, "50 %") · track with a centre mark, filled from the centre to the thumb · the ends' words small under the track, with the bleed hint in the middle (its place kept).
Variants
with or without curves; bleed (px, default 32); format for the readout.
States
resting (50 %); moving (the label emphasised, the fill from the centre); in the bleed area (the thumb back at the middle, dashed, "Release to cancel"); disabled with its reason.
Sizes
Label line 24 px; track as Slider; ends' words --fs-2xs.
When
One control that moves many values together and has no lasting value of its own (scale every control in use, later other whole-face operations).
Combine
A row in an operations section (the Expression panel's Adjust all), under the section heading; its curve buttons belong to its own label line.
Adapt
Full width; the label truncates before the curves or readout would move.
Driven by
onBegin, onPreview(position) (0–100) for every move, onCommit or onCancel: the owner wraps them in a begin/edit/commit/cancel transaction, so the preview is live and applying is one Undo step. onCurve sets the owner's preference; update({ curve, disabled, reason }).
Keyboard & access
A native range labelled by its label and described by what a drag does; arrows, Page Up/Down, Home and End preview; Enter applies; Escape or leaving cancels; the value text is the readout's words. The curves are a named group of toggle buttons with aria-pressed, one Tab stop and arrow keys (Segmented).
Do
Cancel generously: a release at the middle, Escape and a release in the bleed area all apply nothing.
Avoid
Using it for a value that should stay where it's put (use Slider with value).

Segmented control

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
One choice among two to four short options, all visible in one strip that hugs its choices; or, icon only, up to eight choices whose icons say what they are (the easing curves).
Module
studio-ui/controls.ts · Segmented · General
Anatomy
Label, with an optional help tip and, with readout, the chosen choice's name at the right of the label line (where a slider shows its value) (help, changed with setHelp: what the choice is, such as where Colour grade's game grade comes from) · sunken frame · segments (icon and/or label) · the chosen one raised with a signal underline · with reserveNote, a note line under them (what is happening now: loading, a stand-in).
Variants
compact; showLabel: false (named by its group label); reserveNote; iconOnly (each segment its icon alone, its label the accessible name and, unless a title says more, the tooltip; name the chosen one with readout, as the Expression drawer's Curve does); readout; frameless (no sunken frame, for a strip on another control's label line: Adjust all › Intensity's curves, which look, focus and name themselves exactly as the Curve strip does); readoutGutter (the column of a slider's reset kept empty after the readout, so the name lines up with Duration's value above it); quietReason (a reason that is information, such as a dependency on the switch above, keeps the muted note tone, never the warning tone: Curve's "Turn on Animate changes to set these."; Slider, Slider with value, Toggle and Choice list take it too).
States
chosen (aria-pressed), hover, unavailable option (with its reason), the whole group unavailable (one reason in the note line, which can speak for the controls above it too, as Curve's does for Duration; its label and readout muted), a transient note ("Loading that idle") in the reserved line.
Sizes
24 px segments inside a 28 px frame; icon-only segments at least 30 px wide; frameless segments 22 px high. The strip is as wide as its segments.
When
Modes, views and sizes (Both eyes / Single eye; Nodes / Mod data; 512 / 1K / 2K / 4K); icon only, the easing curves (Expression › Transitions › Curve). A varying or longer set, long labels or a numbered set use the Choice list.
Combine
In a page header's actions, a toolbar or a panel section, with its note line above the controls that depend on it.
Adapt
The strip hugs its choices and never wraps or stretches to the panel. Choose icons or a Choice list where the labels wouldn't fit at 300 px.
Driven by
An action per choice; the chosen value from a snapshot; setOptions(choices) when the list changes (rebuilt only when it differs, focus kept on the same choice).
Keyboard & access
A labelled group of toggle buttons (aria-pressed) with one Tab stop (the chosen choice): Left and Right move between the choices (wrapping), Home and End to the ends, Enter or Space chooses; arrows never choose, since a choice may be an edit. A disabled group states its reason in the note line and as the group's description; an icon-only segment is named by its label.
Do
Keep options short and parallel; icon only when every icon is distinct and its name is one hover away.
Avoid
A strip with more than four labelled options or long labels (use the Choice list), icon only for choices an icon can't show, or lists that need search.
See also
c-segmented, c-choice-list

Choice preview

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A picture of a choice drawn in the UI's own palette, for rows whose choices differ in shape or pattern (hairstyles first; brows, makeup, piercings, body kinds and poses later, research/character-customization/choice-previews-design.md). Pictures are diagrams, not photographs: a neutral subject, the choice in one ink, one soft light and one frame per row, so a long cut runs out of the frame and a pixie cut doesn't.
Module
studio-ui/components/choice-preview.ts · previewTile, PreviewSpin, SPIN, installPreviewFilter, previewTokens, PREVIEW_FILTER_IDS · General
Anatomy
Inside a choiceItem (which draws the border and the chosen, hover and focus states): a frame of the flat --pv-ground, bevelled top-right and bottom-left · the picture (a theme-free channel image coloured by an SVG colour matrix per theme from --pv-subject, --pv-ink and --pv-shade) · the label (--fs-2xs, muted, one line) · the prepared-ahead corner mark of the creator's choices.
Variants
Grid sizes S (56 px, label visually hidden: accessible name and tooltip only), M (88 px, the hairstyle default), L (132 px); list (28 px beside the label and source) and details (64 px with the prepared state) rows, see Choice layouts (lib-choice-layouts). Square aspect for hair; 2:1 and 1:2 for later kinds.
States
waiting (the frame and a faint glyph for the kind, never a spinner: the corner mark says the choice is being prepared) · ready (the picture fades in over --dur, at once under reduced motion) · none (no picture possible: the glyph stays, no error in the tile) · turning (every grid size and details, not list rows: the pointer resting on the picture turns it slowly after 400 ms, one turn in 8 s, never under reduced motion; pressing and dragging turns it by hand at once, with the grab cursor; a drag never chooses, a click still does at once; the one picture being turned is drawn live by the preview worker (up to 30 frames a second, tile.setLive(frames)) with the 24-frame strip as the instant fallback; while the strip is still being drawn on first look, a 12 px muted tick on a faint chip in the frame's top-right corner, overlaid, turning only while it waits (still under reduced motion); the still comes back when the pointer leaves) · chosen, hover and focus from the choice item. A picture arriving, failing or turning never moves the layout.
Sizes
A grid of repeat(auto-fill, minmax(size, 1fr)) with 4 px gaps; the tile is its column wide, the frame square, the label 15 px.
When
Rows whose choices differ in shape (the Character panel's hairstyles). Not for colour-only rows (a swatch) and never a substitute for the 3D view, which stays the true preview.
Combine
The Character panel's creator choices put previewTile({ label, glyph }) in a choiceItem (class preview-choice) inside a .choices.previews[data-size] grid; the row's Segmented S/M/L sits above it (the choiceSize.set UI preference, per feature type).
Adapt
Columns follow the panel's width; tiles use content-visibility: auto, so a 283-choice row costs little until scrolled. Forced colours drop the colour matrix (the raw channels still read as shapes) and use system borders.
Driven by
Presentation only: tile.set(url, none), tile.setSpin(strip, frames), tile.spinnable(on) and tile.setMeta(source, state) from the Character context's read-only previews(option, …) row (choice-preview-service.ts); the picture comes from the preview worker or the host's store, keyed by the resolved winner. The turntable strip (24 frames side by side, frame 0 the still) is drawn only for the choice the list wants turning and set as an image only while it turns.
Keyboard & access
The picture is decorative (alt=""); the choice item keeps its name (the label), its description (maker and prepared state) and the listbox keys, with Up and Down moving by the grid's columns.
Do
Keep one frame per row and the tokens only (plus the V's own colour when tinted, later).
Avoid
Realistic renders dropped into slots, a spinner per tile, a picture that changes the tile's size, an error message inside a tile.
See also
lib-choice-list, lib-choice-layouts, c-creator, f-preview-tokens

Stage tag

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A part of the Studio that isn't finished says so, Early access, wherever it is listed or shown, so it is never mistaken for a finished part. Stable parts carry none. The word is used for nothing else ("preview" is the Studio's word for the 3D view). The product shows only what exists: an early-access part is usable today; a planned feature is not listed at all (only with research tools on, as a muted Soon menu tag).
Module
studio-ui/components/stage-tag.ts · stageTag, stageLabel, stageShortLabel · General
Anatomy
Small outlined caps in the signal colour (the info tone), the menu tag's shape: 1 px signal-line border, display face, uppercase, tracked. Never an icon alone.
Variants
Where it sits: a menu entry's stage (Modules menu, Panels flyout, a tab strip's overflow menu), a tab's stage (every panel of an early-access module), a switch's stage (Motion › Hair physics). Any stage other than stable is early access. The long form "Early access" wherever it fits; the short form "Early" only on a condensed tab.
States
Static. Beside a disabled switch it dims with the label (45 %): hierarchy follows usability, so a qualifier is never the brightest thing on a row that can't be used.
Sizes
The 2xs display size; 1.35 line height on a tab, 1.1 inside a menu label, so a tagged row is exactly as tall as an untagged one. It never wraps.
When
An early-access module (Expressions, Poses, Save Explorer) and each place it shows up; an early-access setting inside a stable panel (Hair physics).
Combine
After the label, before any help tip: new Toggle({ label: "Hair physics", stage: "preview", onChange }); { kind: "action", label: module.label, stage: module.stage, … }. ("preview" is the manifest's internal stage ID; the words shown are Early access.) The shell gives every panel of an early-access module its module's stage, so a feature never tags its own tabs.
Adapt
On a tab the tag shows only beside a whole label, so the name never loses room to its qualifier: every tab in the full stage ("Early access"); the active tab in the icons and overflow stages while its label shows whole ("Early"); no tab in the truncated stage. A tab without its tag keeps the words in its name and tooltip ("Expression, Early access"), and the overflow menu tags its entries.
Driven by
The module manifest's stage (platform/api/module.ts); a setting's stage is decided by its panel.
Keyboard & access
Read as part of its control's name: inside a menu entry's and a switch's label; a tab's name gains ", Early access" and its tag is aria-hidden. Colour is never the only signal: the words are the meaning.
Do
Tag every place an early-access part is listed or shown, the same way. Say what is not finished in its help tip ("An early-access setting: how the hair moves hasn't been matched to the game yet").
Avoid
"Preview" as a stage (it means the 3D view); warning colours or badges for a stage (early access isn't a problem); "Beta" (the release channel's word: the product's one stage marker, the accent badge beside the name in the header, never a module's), "Experimental" (a finish's export status) or "Coming soon" for a module; listing features that don't exist yet.
See also
c-context, c-chips

With or without a secondary action; contributed defaults never have Delete.

role=tablist/tab, roving focus; a folded strip is aria-orientation=vertical and its owner moves along it with Up and Down as well as Left and Right; every tab is named by its label and titled by its label and context, so icon-only tabs still say what they are; the more button names the tabs it holds; the focus ring is drawn inside the tab, so a clipped strip never cuts it.

Give every tab an icon (it is what remains). Write tab spacing in logical properties so the vertical strip follows.

Tree view

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A virtualised hierarchy: grouped rows (poses by pack, expressions by source), or recursive nodes of arbitrary depth (sections, clumps, layers). The live specimens compare both forms below.
Module
studio-ui/components/tree-view.ts · TreeView, TREE_ROW_HEIGHT, treeHeightWords, favouriteToggle · General
Anatomy
Frame (owner sized or fitted with maxRows) · empty line · scrolling hierarchy. Recursive nodes: disclosure column, optional colour swatch, label with match highlights, secondary text, badges and optional explicit count. Grouped input retains its group/row layout and trailing action slot. Loading status stays pinned to the frame's corner.
Variants
maxRows (and minRows): the frame fits its visible items up to that many rows, then scrolls, and an empty tree fits its message; sizeBar: { key, defaultRows }: a Size bar under the frame, in whole rows, sets that most (without maxRows, the frame's height; place tree.sizeBar.region); with or without trailing actions (the favourite toggle: outline star off, filled on, named "Add to favourites" or "Remove from favourites"); search highlights; secondary text.
States
Open and closed branches; hover (neutral fill); selected/current (signal fill and left inset); focus-visible (2 px inset focus ring, independent of selection); disabled (focusable, reason as tooltip and description, never activates). Recursive branches select on label click, Enter or Space; the chevron cell (hover fill), a double click on the label and the arrows disclose. With selectable:false, a branch only discloses. On collapse, focus on a descendant returns to its nearest surviving ancestor. Legacy groups still toggle on whole-row click, Enter and Space; legacy leaves still activate on click or Enter. Loading stays pinned; empty groups are hidden in the legacy form.
Sizes
Every item 28 px (TREE_ROW_HEIGHT); recursive levels indent 16 px, reserving a chevron column even on leaves; a branch's disclosure cell is a 24 px × full-row target around its 10 px chevron, without moving the label. Optional swatch 12 × 12 px; when any sibling has one, every sibling reserves the slot so labels line up. Numeric metadata uses count: the same muted monospace count style in grouped and recursive rows; descriptive secondary text keeps the body face. Same border, spacing, focus and selection tokens as grouped rows.
When
Long grouped lists where one click applies the item. Short ordered lists use the Ordered list.
Combine
A Search field above with onArrowDown: () => tree.focus(); rows carry trailingState and the owner's onKey maps F to the favourite toggle.
Adapt
Only the items in view plus a margin, the focused item and recursive ancestors are rendered. Closed child providers are never called. Items are reused by kind and stable ID. Legacy secondary text still hides below 320 px; recursive short metadata stays visible at every width, left-aligned after the label as in grouped rows, and shrinks before the label. As in grouped rows, a tooltip (label · secondary text) appears only where secondary text may be cut, or gives a disabled reason; accessible names carry label, secondary text, count and badges. Swatches supplement the label, never replace it.
Driven by
Legacy: update({ groups, expanded, current, loading }). Recursive: update({ nodes, expanded, selected, loading }), where TreeNodeData.children is an array or synchronous provider; nodes accept secondary, swatch, count and selectable. Both report onActivate(id), onToggle(id, expanded), onHover(item|null) and onFocus(item); item references carry kind, ID and parent context, not mutable data. The owner controls selection and expansion. signal withdraws listeners/observations and clears hover. Existing remember, scrollToItem, focusItem, onKey and onMenu work at every visible level.
Keyboard & access
The WAI-ARIA tree pattern: one tab stop, explicit levels, sibling positions and sizes; aria-expanded only on branches; aria-selected on selectable nodes, with focus separate from selection. Recursive branches own a role=group which owns their rendered direct children; ancestors remain rendered during virtualisation. Up/Down and Home/End traverse visible nodes, Right opens or enters, Left closes or goes to the parent, Enter/Space select recursive nodes, typing a letter finds the next matching visible label (wrapping). Shift+F10/Menu opens the owner's context menu. Names include metadata, badges and explicit counts; decorative swatches are hidden from accessibility. Loading/empty messages stay outside the tree.
Do
Keep IDs stable and unique across recursive nodes. Give disabled rows a plain reason. Use synchronous child providers for lazy snapshot projections, and retain expansion and selection in the owner. Wire hover/focus to inspection without selecting.
Avoid
Rendering closed descendants; loading files inside child providers; selecting on arrow navigation; using colour as the only identity.

Size bar

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
A bar under a list, tree or scroll region that the person drags to make it taller or shorter, remembered across reloads. The Direction dial's resize bar is one too, for a drawing (it sets the drawing's height, reports its width with scale, and its owner keeps the size with setChosen).
Module
studio-ui/components/size-bar.ts · SizeBar, SIZE_BAR_STEP, SIZE_BAR_TITLE, chooseHeight, snapHeight, rowWords, clampHeight, panelLimit · General
Anatomy
The region (its frame unchanged) · right under it, 1 px below its frame so the focus ring reads as the bar's own, a full-width 12 px bar with a short centred grip line (36 × 3 px, --line-strong). The two sit in one size-region the owner places where the region would go. Tooltip "Drag to resize · double-click to reset" (SIZE_BAR_TITLE, the dial's bar says the same).
Variants
Generic: new SizeBar({ label, target, key, minHeight, defaultHeight }) sets the target's height; fit makes it as tall as its content up to the height (max-height: the Save Explorer's node tree); snap stops a drag at whole rows; valueText says the height in words (rowWords: rows). Built into the Tree view: sizeBar: { key, defaultRows }, in whole rows. With maxRows (the Start from list, the Poses tree) the chosen height replaces it as the most the frame fits to, and the tree still fits fewer rows (a search that leaves a few); without it the frame is the chosen height, defaultRows by default.
States
rest (grip line neutral); hover and dragging (the grip line turns signal and widens to 48 px, nothing else moves); focus-visible (a 2 px inset ring round the bar); at the default (no height remembered) or chosen.
Sizes
Bar 12 px tall, the region's full width; the resize cursor (ns-resize) over it. Keyboard step one row (a tree's 28 px, SIZE_BAR_STEP; the save tree's 26 px), and a tree's drags snap to whole rows. Never under minHeight (a tree: minRows), never over, while resizing, the panel's visible height less the bar (panelLimit). What the region holds (a tree's rows, a fitted list's content) caps only what shows, never the chosen height: enlarging a list whose groups are closed, or that a search is filtering, changes nothing, and the kept height comes back when the rows do (chooseHeight). A shrink starts from what shows.
When
A list people come back to that is useful both compact and tall: the Expression drawer's Start from list, the Poses tree, the Save Explorer's node tree. Not for a region that fills its panel (the panel is the size), menus, popovers or dialogs, nor several bars stacked in one view.
Combine
Under the region in its section: const tree = new TreeView({ label: "Start from", maxRows: 6, minRows: 3, sizeBar: { key: "expressions:start-from" }, … }), then place tree.sizeBar.region instead of tree.element.
Adapt
Dragging moves only the bar and what is under the region: the region's top stays put. While the bar is held, a shrinking region leaves its lost height as a reserve under the bar, so a panel scrolled to its end never pulls what is above it down. That reserve goes when the drag ends, so a panel scrolled to its very end settles once then (as it does at once for Up on the keyboard there): the direct result of the person's own resize, accepted, and never phantom space left behind. A narrower panel changes nothing; a shorter one lowers the most a resize can reach.
Driven by
Presentation state, never Undo: the chosen height is remembered under the bar's view key in the workspace's sizes UI preference (size.set {key, height}, view-state.ts size), written when a gesture ends and only when it chose something new; onResize(height, final) for owners that keep it themselves.
Keyboard & access
Its own tab stop, role=separator with aria-orientation=horizontal, named "Resize <label>", with the height as its value: in rows for a list ("6 rows, default", "7 and a half rows"), pixels only for a generic region; aria-valuenow and its bounds stay in px. Down and Up enlarge and shrink by a row, Home and End go to the smallest and largest, Delete or Backspace returns to the default. A drag ends on release, a lost pointer capture or a second press; Escape during it goes back to where it started. Double-click returns to the default.
Do
Give it a stable view key per region, so each list keeps its own height; say the height in rows for a list.
Avoid
A bar under a region that already fills its panel; resizing from the top edge, which moves what is above; a hand-built grip; raw pixels in a list's value text.
See also
lib-tree-view, lib-direction-dial, lib-view-state

Remembered view state

Implemented

Scripts build this specimen from the production component.

What
What a person folded or opened and where each scroll container was, remembered across reloads: the same rows come back at the top, and a folded section stays folded.
Module
studio-ui/view-state.ts, scroll-anchor.ts · RememberedSet, ScrollMemory, VIEW_KEY, holdScroll, revealInView · General
Anatomy
A view key per foldable control or scroll container (<namespace>:<path> or <namespace>.<path>: character:row:head/hair, expressions.mouth, panel:character) · data-view-key on the elements a scroll position can anchor on · a scroll anchor: the element at the top edge, its clip offset (how many px of it are scrolled past the edge), up to four elements before it and the plain scroll position.
Variants
Folds: GroupSection (its key), the Character panel's headings, rows and author groups, a tree's groups (RememberedSet). Scroll: every panel (panel:<id>, the dock group's body), every TreeView (tree:<label>, virtualised), any container with new ScrollMemory(element, key).
States
nothing stored (the control's default); stored; stored for a control not shown yet (kept until it shows); a restore pending (waiting for its content), exact, fallen back to an element before it, or dropped because the person scrolled first.
Sizes
At most 192 open states per namespace and 512 in all, and 64 scroll anchors; the least recently set go first.
When
Every foldable heading, row or group and every container that scrolls a list people come back to. Transient lists (a menu, a popover) aren't remembered.
Combine
Library components do it themselves; a feature names the keys. Section blocks (section()) and GroupSections carry their key as data-view-key; give rows of your own a data-view-key so the scroll position can come back to them.
Adapt
Resizing never loses the place: a height-only change keeps the scroll position; a width change (the content reflows) puts the anchor from before the resize back at minus its clip offset, through a whole splitter drag or window resize, and not while the person is scrolling. A panel floated, docked or re-laid out restores from the anchor recorded as its old container went. Content that loads later (a catalogue, a tree's rows, mods) is waited for: each change tries the restore again until the anchor is exactly where it was (30 s at most). A missing anchor falls back to the nearest element before it that is still there (an element around it keeps how far it was scrolled past), then to the plain position.
Driven by
Presentation state, never Undo and not part of a saved layout: the workspace's expanded, scroll and sizes UI preferences (expanded.set {keys, expanded}, scroll.set {key, anchor}, size.set {key, height}, the last for a Size bar's height), so a verification workspace keeps its own and every layout shows the same state. Recorded on scroll (debounced), when a container is rebuilt and before the page is hidden.
Keyboard & access
Restoring never moves focus. A wheel, touch, key or pointer press in the container drops a pending restore, so the person's own scrolling always wins. Choosing something in a list never moves the view (holdScroll: what is at the top edge stays there for a moment, whatever the choice rebuilds or focuses); bringing an element into view (revealInView) scrolls only its own container, as little as needed, and never during a restore or hold.
Do
Key by what the element is (its slot, section or item ID), not its position or title that can change.
Avoid
Remembering pixel positions alone; restoring after the person has started scrolling; keys in browser storage outside the workspace.

studio-ui/components/conflict-notice.ts · ConflictNotice · General
Anatomy
A warning state line · the lead-in Changed in another window. and the owner's sentence (what it is, what differs, the question) · one row of small buttons: Keep mine, Use other window's, Keep both · for Keep mine and Use other window's, a confirm popover anchored to the button (c-confirm): its title, one sentence naming the document and what is discarded (“Use the other window's version of the preset “Smoky”? Your changes to it here are discarded.”), Cancel and the danger-styled action.
Variants
with Keep both (a V, a preset: a copy can be made) or without (a collection's name or list).
States
hidden (no conflict waits: it takes no room), shown, a way out unavailable with its reason (the Button's own), asking (Keep mine's or Use other window's confirm popover open, focus on Cancel). Keep both never asks: it loses nothing.
Sizes
Full width of its section; buttons small, 8 px apart, wrapping under the sentence.
When
First in the section that owns the document, only while a conflict on it waits: the Character panel's “Your V”, the Presets panel under the collection's name. Never a dialog, toast or status-bar line.
Combine
const notice = new ConflictNotice({ onResolve: keep => owner.resolve(keep), capability: keep => owner.capability(keep) }) placed first in the section, then notice.update(conflict ? { message, keepBoth, subject } : null) on each paint; subject names the document in the confirmations (“the preset “Smoky””, “this V”). onResolve runs only once the person confirms, and only if the same conflict still waits.
Adapt
The sentence wraps; the buttons wrap under it, in order.
Driven by
The owner's snapshot (the sentence and whether a copy can be made) and its typed resolution action or request.
Keyboard & access
A group named “Changed in another window”, polite live region; each button's tooltip says what it keeps, and Keep mine's and Use other window's that they ask first. The confirmation is an alertdialog described by its sentence; focus starts on Cancel, so a stray Enter discards nothing; Escape or Cancel returns focus to the button.
Do
Say what differs in plain words, with no nested brackets (“(its name: “Smoky glow” there)”); keep editing available while it shows; name the document and what goes in each confirmation.
Avoid
Blocking the panel; a dialog; Keep both where no copy can be made; a way out that throws a version away in one click; “Use theirs”, which suggests another person.

Implemented

What
The full-width band under the header for a workspace state the person must act on or wait out: this window read-only, taking over, waiting, handing over or kept ([t-read-only-window]); changes not backed up on this computer ([t-unprotected]); restoring that is taking a while, or restored changes waiting for a missing save ([t-recovering]).

Anatomy
A warning state line the width of the window, under the header · the message, in semibold, whole · its ways out as small labelled buttons, in the order the owner gives: Use it here; Try again, then Export this window's copy (kept or not backed up); Try again, then Use restored or Export this window's copy (restoring); Import save… and Discard those changes, which asks first in place (c-confirm).
Variants
By state: a message alone (taking over, waiting, handing over, lost connection), or a message with one or two ways out. Each way out has one label and one tooltip everywhere (WORKSPACE_NOTICE_ACTIONS); the three Try agains say in their tooltips what they try.
States
hidden (no state: the band takes no room), shown, asking (Discard those changes' confirm popover open, focus on Cancel), waiting to open (a gesture is in progress: a closed notice stays closed until it ends, an open one changes in place).
Sizes

When
Only for a workspace state that needs the person, and for as long as it lasts. Never for a transient moment (restoring's first seconds are the status bar's line), never for one document's state (a conflict is the owning panel's [lib-conflict-notice]), never a dialog or a toast.
Combine
const notice = new WorkspaceNotice({ onAction: action => run[action]() }) placed between the header and the dock, then notice.update(state, { deferOpen: gestureInProgress }) on each paint, where state is { message, actions } or null (app.ts workspaceNoticeState derives it from the lease and the outbox). onAction hears Discard those changes only once it is confirmed.
Adapt
One rule at every width: the message, whole (it wraps, never ends in an ellipsis), then the buttons beside it where they fit, on the row under it where they don't (its own width narrower than 720 px, always), wrapping, never shrunk to icons.
Driven by
The owner's derived state (the lease's message and offers, the outbox's unprotected and recovering state) and its actions: the lease's take-over and retry, the documents' backup, restore and discard, and the files' export and save import.
Keyboard & access
A polite status region, so a new state is announced once; the buttons are ordinary buttons in reading order, each with its tooltip as its description. Discard those changes' confirmation is an alertdialog with focus on Cancel; Escape or Cancel returns focus to the button.
Do
Say what happened and what could happen, then offer each way on the message names, labelled.
Avoid
Opening it for a moment, or mid-gesture; an icon alone for any of its buttons; a message that names a step with no button for it; discarding in one click; repeating it in a toast or the status bar.
