Communicating state

Four kinds of state must stay intelligible: the portable recipe/collection (authored work), the browser workspace (draft autosave, selections, view), immutable SQLite library revisions, and exported files. These patterns keep them apart in words and placement.

Saved as you work, and versions

Implemented
No version yetSavedChanged since last versionNewer version savedWorking…Version 3

Changed since version 3: 2 presets. Save version makes version 4.

What
Work saves itself to the library as you go (profiles design §2.2), so nothing waits for a save to be kept. Save version (Ctrl+S, the header's Save) keeps a named version that you can return to and that older XF Studio versions read. One save status (UI-89): the library chip compares the collection with the last version saved (no version yet, saved, changed since the last version, or behind a newer version saved elsewhere), and its tooltip says what changed. The status bar speaks about saving only when it has a problem.
When
One place: the header, beside the preset name (G3, one place per state). The Library panel explains the consequence in a sentence; the Presets panel doesn't repeat the chip.
Combine
Save version records a new immutable version from the library's own copy of the collection; edits made while it runs are kept. Export collection and the build plan save a version first and say so. Check and Build read the collection as it is now, latest edits included, and save no version.
Adapt
Header chip hides below 720 px; the Library panel's sentence keeps the information.
Driven by
status.workspace, library.summary().draft.revision vs summaries[].revision.
Avoid
A second chip for the same state in a panel; claiming more than the comparison with the last version knows (its tooltip says what changed: "the collection's name or order", "2 presets").

A workspace open in another window

Implemented
XF
Preset 1Read-only
This workspace is open in another window.
This workspace is open in another window. Choose Use it here to edit in this window.
Taking over from the other window…
Waiting for the other window to finish saving. Close the other window to continue.
Handing this workspace to another window…
Your latest changes couldn't be saved, so this window kept the workspace. Try again, or export this window's copy to keep them.
This window lost its connection to XF Studio, so it can't save here. Reload the window to continue.
What
One window writes a workspace at a time (the workspace lease). Another window on the same workspace opens read-only, and says so in three places that agree: a full-width notice directly under the header, in the warning tone, says “This workspace is open in another window.” beside one small Use it here button; the header's library chip reads Read-only (it makes no claim about saving); and every editing control in the panels shows as unavailable, with the same reason as its tooltip, through the ordinary unavailable-command pattern (t-disabled). Use it here asks the other window to finish saving and hand over; the notice says “Taking over from the other window…”, then, if the other window hasn't finished after a moment, “Waiting for the other window to finish saving. Close the other window to continue.” The window then restarts with the workspace as the other window left it. The window that hands over says “Handing this workspace to another window…” while it saves, then shows the read-only notice itself. If its last changes can't be saved, it hands nothing over: it keeps the workspace and its edits, the notice says “Your latest changes couldn't be saved, so this window kept the workspace. Try again, or export this window's copy to keep them.” with the two ways on it names, Try again and Export this window's copy (the recovery export: the collection as this window shows it, changes the library doesn't have included, written to a file without saving or reading anything, so it works although the library couldn't take them), and the other window keeps waiting. A window that loses its connection to XF Studio (or never got a lease) says “This window lost its connection to XF Studio, so it can't save here. Reload the window to continue.” and is read-only.
When
Only while this window doesn't hold its workspace; a window that holds it shows none of this. Never a dialog or toast: the state lasts as long as the window is read-only, and the window stays readable. Prompts that would write settings or data (the 3D view's first-run setup card, the onboarding offer, the desktop welcome) don't open in a read-only window.
Combine
Replaces the saving problem line (t-saved), which a read-only window never has, since it writes nothing. What the port still allows, or what only changes this window's own view, stays available: panel tabs and layout, expanders, help tips, links, search fields, the UV map's view buttons, Open mod package, Keyboard & mouse, Settings' theme and input preferences, diagnostic mode, Report a problem, Help and Activity. A control the port allows records its port capability with capabilityScope; a view-only control carries data-read-safe; Help and Activity are read-safe panels; everything else in a panel is unavailable. A refused dispatch that still reaches the application is a warning toast that fades.
Adapt
The Workspace notice component's one rule at every width (lib-workspace-notice): the message, whole (it wraps, never ends in an ellipsis), then its labelled buttons beside it where they fit, on the row under it where they don't (narrower than 720 px, always), never shrunk to icons. A window that opens read-only shows it from the first paint; a window that hands over gains it once, when it becomes read-only, and it stays until the window holds its workspace again. Its unavailable controls fade to .7, not the usual .45: they are unavailable because of where the workspace is open, not because of what they show, so their names stay readable (f-contrast).
Driven by
status.lease (phase, writable, message, canTakeOver); workspace.dispatch({ kind: "workspace.takeOver" }); the controls' unavailable state from the lease's refusal (workspace.capability).
Avoid
Taking the workspace by time or without the other window's release; a status-bar line or a panel notice repeating it; controls that look enabled and only refuse when used; calling it an error.

Changed in another window

Implemented

Your V

Changed in another window. You changed this V here too. Which version should it keep?

From a save (feminine)

Your V

Changed in another window. You changed this V here too. Which version should it keep?

From a save (feminine)

Your V

From a save (feminine)

Changed in another window. Undo starts here.

Changed in another window. You changed the preset “Smoky” here too (its name: “Smoky glow” there, its makeup). Which version should it keep?

Changed in another window. You changed the collection “Night market set” here too (the order of its presets). Which version should it keep?

Use the other window's version

Use the other window's version of the preset “Smoky”? Your changes to it here are discarded.

Keep this window's version

Keep this window's version of this V? The other window's changes to it are discarded.

What
A document this window changed was changed in another window too, before this window's change reached the library. Nothing is written over either version. The owning panel says so first in the section the document belongs to (the Character panel's “Your V” for a V; the Presets panel, under the collection's name, for a preset or the collection), in the warning tone: what it is, what differs (a preset's name, with the other window's name after a colon, never in nested brackets: “(its name: “Smoky glow” there)”; its makeup, or that the other window removed it; a collection's name, which presets it lists or their order), and the question. It offers the three ways out, each one small button: Keep mine saves this window's version over the other's; Use other window's shows the other window's version here instead, and this window's changes go (never “Use theirs”: the other version is another window's, not another person's). Each of those two throws a version away for good (the library keeps no earlier copy of either), so each asks first, in place (c-confirm), naming the document and what goes: “Use the other window's version of the preset “Smoky”? Your changes to it here are discarded.” with Cancel, which has focus, and Use other window's. Keep both loses nothing and acts at once: it keeps this window's version as a copy beside the other (a V's copy is named “… (this window)” and joins every profile that lists the V; a preset's copy joins its collection) and shows the other window's version here. Several conflicts on one collection show one notice each, oldest first. While one waits, Save version, Check, Build and Export collection say why they wait (“Choose which version to keep first, in the Presets panel.”). Each button's tooltip says what it keeps. Editing carries on while the notice shows: further changes join this window's version. After Use other window's or Keep both, or when a document this window hadn't changed is changed elsewhere, the section's status line says “Changed in another window. Undo starts here.” until the next change made here; Undo can't go back past it.
When
Only while a conflict on that document waits, in the panel that owns the document, and only there: never a dialog, toast or status-bar line. A conflict stored before the window closed shows again when the document is next shown. The status line's note is the one transient part, and it takes the status line's fixed height, so it moves nothing.
Combine
Sits first in the owning section, above the section's own lines; the section's other controls keep working. The three buttons sit in the order mine, theirs, both on one row. Keep both is offered where a copy can be made (a V, a preset); otherwise (a collection's name or list) only the first two show. Built from the Conflict notice component. Built from the state line (warning tone), a strong lead-in and the small button.
Adapt
At 300 px the sentence wraps under its lead-in and the three buttons share one row; narrower, they wrap to a second row, never shrinking their labels. The notice's height follows its text; it appears and goes only when a conflict comes or is resolved, never while editing.
Driven by
CharacterContextActions.snapshot().conflict (message, keepBoth) and .elsewhere; character.resolveConflict with keep = mine, theirs or both; for presets and collections library.summary().draft.conflicts (id, message, keepBoth) and the request resolveConflict with conflict and keep; the outbox's conflicts (profiles design §2.2).
Keyboard & access
The notice is a group labelled by its lead-in and announced politely when it appears; the buttons are ordinary buttons, reachable by Tab in reading order, each with its tooltip as its description. Keep mine's and Use other window's confirmation is an alertdialog described by its sentence, with focus on Cancel, so a stray Enter discards nothing; Escape or Cancel returns focus to the button.
Avoid
Choosing for the person (merging silently, or the newest edit winning); a way out that discards a version in one click; the words conflict, revision or sync; a modal that blocks the other panels; repeating the notice in the status bar or a toast.

Changes not backed up on this computer

Implemented
XF
Preset 1Changed since last version
Your latest changes couldn't be backed up on this computer. If XF Studio closes before your library has them, they could be lost.
Your latest changes are still being backed up on this computer. Keep XF Studio open until your library has them, or export this window's copy to keep them.
Storage on this computer is full, so your latest changes couldn't be backed up. Free up some space, then try again. Keep XF Studio open until your library has them, or export this window's copy to keep them.
Your latest changes couldn't be backed up on this computer. If XF Studio closes before your library has them, they could be lost.
What
Every change is held in memory the moment it is made and backed up on this computer within about a quarter of a second, before the library has it, so it can be restored after a crash or a closed window. When that backup can't be written (storage is full, or the desktop app couldn't write its file), the window says so in the full-width notice under the header, and says what could happen: “Your latest changes couldn't be backed up on this computer. If XF Studio closes before your library has them, they could be lost.”, with Try again (back them up again) and Export this window's copy (keep a copy now, without the library). Editing never stops and nothing is held back: changes still go to the library as usual, and the notice goes once a later backup is written or the library has those changes. A desktop backup taking longer than two seconds says it is still being backed up; only a failed write says it couldn't be. When storage is known to be full, the notice names it and asks for space to be freed before trying again. It never says “protected”, which reads as security.
When
Only while a change still waiting for the library has a failed backup or a desktop backup taking longer than two seconds. A read-only window shows its read-only notice instead (t-read-only-window): it backs up nothing.
Combine
The Workspace notice component (lib-workspace-notice) with two small labelled buttons. It opens when a backup fails or takes longer than two seconds, but never in the middle of a gesture or slider adjustment: it waits until that ends, so the panels don't move under the pointer, and then stays until a later backup is written or the library has the changes. Nothing else repeats it; the library chip still says whether work is saved in the library.
Adapt
The workspace notice's one rule: one line where it fits; narrower than 720 px the message takes its own row, whole, and the labelled buttons the row under it, wrapping. Its height follows its text. The panels below move only when the band opens or closes for this state, never during a gesture.
Driven by
status.outbox.unprotected and its reason (pending, failed or storage-full); documents.protect for Try again; collection.exportWindowCopy for Export this window's copy.
Avoid
Buttons shrunk to bare icons; truncating the message; opening it mid-gesture; blocking edits, a dialog, or saying the work is lost (it isn't: it still reaches the library); the vague “aren't protected”; calling it an error.

Restoring changes from the last session

Implemented
XF
Preset 1Changed since last version
Restoring changes from your last session…3D view 2K · ready
Restoring changes from your last session is taking a while.
Restoring changes from your last session is taking a while.
Some restored changes need a game save that's no longer on this computer. Import it again, or discard them.
Restoring changes from your last session is taking a while.
Restoring changes from your last session is taking a while.
Some restored changes need a game save that's no longer on this computer. Import it again, or discard them.
Discard those changes

Discard the restored changes that need that game save? What they changed goes back to the library's version, and they can't be got back.

What
When the Studio opens, changes from the last session that hadn't reached the library yet are sent again first, and what they change can't be edited until the library has answered (an edit made before then could otherwise land over a newer version unseen). That usually takes a moment and shows nothing. If it takes longer than a second, the status bar's line says “Restoring changes from your last session…” (its fixed height moves nothing), and the activity message's idle “Ready” gives way while it does, so the bar never says both. After about five seconds the workspace notice under the header opens: it says it is taking a while and offers a way on: Try again (abandon the attempt that is stuck and send them again now) and, only where it is safe, Use restored (its tooltip: “Keep working on the restored version”); where it isn't safe, Export this window's copy instead, so a copy can be kept without waiting for the library. Safe means the library hadn't taken the restored change when this window read it, so new edits simply follow it. When a restored change needs a game save (a V's source) that is no longer in the library or anywhere on this computer, the notice says so, with Import save… (the usual save import; importing the same save sends the waiting changes and shows the V again) and Discard those changes, which can't be undone, so it asks first in place (c-confirm): “Discard the restored changes that need that game save? What they changed goes back to the library's version, and they can't be got back.”, with focus on Cancel.
When
Only while restored changes wait: the status bar's line from one second after opening while they do; the notice, with its actions, once it has taken about five seconds, and until the restore is resolved; the missing-save notice whenever a change waits for a save nothing holds. The notice never opens in the middle of a gesture or slider adjustment: it waits until that ends. A read-only window shows its read-only notice instead (t-read-only-window), and the unprotected-changes notice (t-unprotected) takes the band while it applies.
Combine
The Workspace notice component (lib-workspace-notice), as t-unprotected and t-read-only-window. Only the editing controls of what is being restored refuse, each with its reason (t-disabled); everything else keeps working, importing a save included. Nothing is ever unlocked by a timer: only Use restored, offered where it is safe, unlocks anything before the library answers.
Adapt
The workspace notice's one rule at every width: one line where it fits; narrower than 720 px the message takes its own row, whole, and the buttons the row under it, labelled and wrapping, never shrunk to icons. The panels below move only when the notice opens (after about five seconds, or for a missing save) and when the state is resolved; the first seconds move nothing.
Driven by
status.outbox.recovering (shown, long, safe, missing): shown without long is the status bar's line, long or missing the notice; documents.retryRecovery for Try again, documents.keepRestored for Use restored, savedV.import for Import save…, documents.discardWaiting for Discard those changes (once confirmed), collection.exportWindowCopy for Export this window's copy.
Keyboard & access
The status bar's line and the notice are polite status regions; the notice's buttons are ordinary buttons in reading order. Discard those changes' confirmation is an alertdialog with focus on Cancel.
Avoid
Unlocking edits after a timeout; a dialog or toast; the words sync, replay or recovery; saying the changes are lost (they aren't: they are still being sent); opening the band for the moment a normal restore takes, or mid-gesture; an icon alone for any of its buttons; discarding in one click.

Undo, recovery and view changes

Implemented
What
Undo follows what you last edited: a preset or a V (the editing context, profiles design §3.7). Each preset and each V keeps its own steps (content edits, one step per gesture or slider drag); the header's Undo and Redo, Ctrl+Z and the History panel step whichever you last edited, and name it (“Changes to Smoky.”, the History summary “Smoky · 3 steps”). View and lighting changes have their own Undo. The Character panel's Undo (UI-81), and Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y anywhere in it but a text box, always step the shown V's creator choices and Clothing, in order. Recovery (restore a removed preset, reopen a previous collection or a recent draft) is separate, and panels, layouts and theme are never undoable and never in recipes.
When
Toasts offer the matching scope: “Undo” after layer removal or reset, “Restore” after preset removal, “Reopen previous” after opening or importing a collection.
Combine
Menus group view commands under their own view heading, after the target's edits. Removal commands say how to get it back, verb first: “Undo with Ctrl+Z” or “Restore from the Presets panel”. Parallel objects share verbs: layers and presets both Move up and Move down.
Adapt
The same wording in toasts, menus and the palette at every size.
Driven by
history.undo capability; preset.edit restore; collection.recover; views never enter the look history.

Async work and cancellation

Implemented

Step 3 of 5: Converting 2 looks…

What
Busy states show the application's progress message. Once the host reports a stage, the stage line (“Step 3 of 5: Converting 2 looks…”) replaces the starting line and the bar sits at the middle of that step. Where the server cannot cancel, the UI says so instead of offering a Cancel that lies.
When
Library requests, package Check/Build, imports. Collection edits are paused while a library request runs; layer editing continues during a save.
Combine
Collection edits pause (disabled with a reason) while a library request runs; layer editing continues during a save.
Adapt
Progress lives in the panel that started it and in the status bar.
Driven by
library.summary().busy/progress, request capabilities (cancellable: false in request descriptors).

Disabled with a reason

Implemented
Select a layer before exporting a mask.
What
Every unavailable command explains itself with the application's reason, in the menu pattern (UI-84): an unavailable button stays focusable (aria-disabled) and shows its reason as a tip on focus, hover or tap; menus, palette entries and note lines show it as text.
When
Always. If the application gives no reason, that is an API gap to report, not a reason to hide the command.
Combine
The same reason text appears in every entry point for the same action.
Adapt
Reasons wrap under controls; they are never truncated.
Driven by
capability(...).reason and code (missing_target, busy, limit, invalid_value, incompatible_mode, asset_unavailable, not_ready, needs_input).

Errors and recovery

Implemented
Library

Your latest changes are still on their way to the library. Try Save version again in a moment.

What
Refusals and errors say what happened, confirm what was kept, and offer the specific recovery: a change made in another window too is resolved with Keep mine or Use other window's (t-conflict); a stale library list offers Check the library again; invalid imports change nothing; failed makeup textures keep the last complete ones and offer Try again. A refusal is a warning; only a real failure is an error, with its reference and Report this problem.
When
Any refused dispatch or failed request. Errors never silently retry.
Combine
An error toast and an Activity entry for every failure; the panel that started the request keeps its last error until the next attempt.
Adapt
Toasts cap their width; the Activity log keeps the full text.
Driven by
{ ok:false, code, message } outcomes; conflict and stale_result codes add recovery actions.

files.package.freshness, status.glitter[].current.

A pointer drag, wheel burst or slider drag is one transaction: one Undo step on completion; Escape, pointer cancel or focus loss restores the start. The status bar says “Gesture in progress · Esc cancels” or “Adjusting · Esc restores”.

Panel moves cancel an active viewport gesture first so a layout change never commits a half-finished edit.

Terminology

Rule
Preset
One complete look; one choice in the single in-game eye-makeup selector (plus Off).
3D view
Where your V is shown in 3D, and what XF Studio prepares from your game files to show it: never “3D preview”, “head view” or “the preview”. Preview quality and Preview only keep the word, which means the 3D view.
Settings › Game
Your game folder, mod manager and WolvenKit's setup: never “Game & tools”, “Local setup” or “Build setup”. Your own copy of WolvenKit is chosen in Settings › Tools.
Layer
One shape with colour, opacity and finish inside a preset. Top of the list = front.
Finish
Matte, Satin, Metallic, Shimmer, Glitter, Glossy, Colour-shifting: one name each, everywhere. Other names (foil, pearl, wet look, duochrome) only in tooltips and search. Satin is shown for the internal “regular”.
Draft
A collection in your library that was never saved as a version. Work saves itself to the library as you go. Recent drafts lists the ones not open now; each row says Draft · no version yet. A collection changed since its last version stays under Saved collections.
Version N
The neutral library chip when version N couldn't be read back for comparison. It makes no claim about changes; its tooltip explains, and the next library refresh tries again.
Reopen
The one name for showing a collection you had open again: Reopen previous (the toast after opening or importing one), Reopen previous collection (the palette, the Presets panel's menu) and Reopen (a recent draft's row). Never “Recover”, “Undo open” or “Show the previous collection”.
Other window's
In a conflict, the version another window of XF Studio saved: Use other window's, never “Use theirs” (it isn't another person's).
Backed up
A change held on this computer before the library has it (within about a quarter of a second). A slow backup says it is still being written; a failed one says what could happen until the library has the changes. To keep or share a separate file, use Export collection; never “protected”, which reads as security.
Library · version
Explicit, immutable saves in your library (version 1, 2…; internally revisions). “Save version”, never just “Save file”; work itself saves to the library as you go.
Collection file · recipe file · build plan
Portable editable data; a build plan is compiler input — none is a mod.
Mod package · Check · Build
Check lists what can be packaged (no files). Build creates your own mod files and checks them; the result says plainly that they are not tested in game and not installed.
Preview only
A browser look that Build cannot turn into mod files yet.
Preview context
The V's creator options (skin, hair, eyes, brows, piercings, makeup…) and the 3D view's toggles: which V the makeup is shown on, never authoring, a save or a package.
What
User-facing words. Internal identifiers (regular, iridescent, xfas/…) never appear in the UI.
When
All labels, messages and docs.

Accessibility checklist

Rule
What
Text ≥4.5:1 and control boundaries ≥3:1 in both themes; visible focus on everything; every icon-only control named; disabled reasons in text; menus/tabs/lists follow ARIA patterns; live regions for results; reduced motion honoured; forced-colors fallbacks; no information by colour alone.
When
Every change. Verify light and dark at 1600 px and 900 px, keyboard-only.

Rules for new UI work

Rule
  1. Mount through createTrustedStudioBootstrap; views receive only StudioPresentationPort (enforced by tests/studio-ui-boundary.test.ts).
  2. Put validation, Undo, persistence and async policy in an application action first; then build the control, menu entry and palette command on it.
  3. Read with port.editor, library.summary(), previewState() and status while repainting; never mutate what you read; snapshot() clones everything and is for diagnostics.
  4. Show capabilities and reasons from the application; never duplicate limits or eligibility in the view (descriptor ranges drive sliders).
  5. Device adapters own canvases, Three, workers, files and network; the view only rehosts viewports and calls ports.
  6. Every new user-visible capability: action/catalogue entry, capability inventory, boundary test, this guide (pattern + status), both themes, keyboard path.
  7. Record unavoidable exceptions with owner and removal criterion in research/authoring/ui-architecture-boundary.md.
What
How to extend the Studio without re-coupling presentation and core.
When
Every feature. The guide is regenerated by tools/build-style-guide.ts from the same CSS and components; tests fail if it falls out of sync.
